It’s official: The general election to represent Washington’s 3rd Congressional District has begun.
I’m Congresswoman Marie Gluesenkamp Perez, officially the Democratic Nominee for Congress, running in one of the closest districts in the country.
https://secure.actblue.com/donate/mgpvf-dsg-email? [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/mgpvf-dsg-email?]
If you’re with me, please help me kick off the general election by pitching in $50, $25, $10, or even just $1. [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/mgpvf-dsg-email?]
DONATE NOW [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/mgpvf-dsg-email?]
In 2024, I won this seat by less than four percentage points. Donald Trump carried the district by the same margin.
That makes me one of just a handful of members of Congress to win a House seat in a district carried by Trump.
Republicans cannot maintain control of the House if they don’t win here this November.
That’s why national Republicans, including Elon Musk, have announced plans to spend vast sums to defeat me.
This is the part where they try to overwhelm us: More money, more ads, more outside groups trying to define this race and buy themselves a House seat.
But I didn’t get into this to follow the rules of a rigged system. I’m not a career politician.
I’m an auto repair shop owner, a mom, and a wife who believes the people of Washington deserve a representative who actually understands work, struggle, and responsibility.
And I believe we can win this thing. But only if we don’t slow down now.
The general election starts now, and we have to hit the ground running. So I’m asking you: Can you pitch in to help us start this next phase strong? [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/mgpvf-dsg-email?]

Now that we’re officially in the general election, all eyes will be on this race. And we need to be ready for what’s coming.
Let’s show them that our district can’t be bought — it’s built by working people who are ready to stand up.
-Marie Gluesenkamp Perez

But I didn’t get into this to follow the rules of a rigged system. I’m not a career politician. I’m an auto repair shop owner, a mom, and a wife who believes the people of Washington deserve a representative who actually understands work, struggle, and responsibility. And I believe we can win this thing. But only if we don’t slow down now. The general election starts now, and we have to hit the ground running. So I’m asking you: Can you pitch in to help us start this next phase strong? [?] DONATE NOW [?] Now that we’re officially in the general election, all eyes will be on this race. And we need to be ready for what’s coming. Let’s show them that our district can’t be bought — it’s built by working people who are ready to stand up. -Marie Gluesenkamp Perez Marie for Congress PO Box 1164 Washougal, WA 98671 United States If you believe you received this message in error or wish to no longer receive email from us, please unsubscribe: .

name: Mark Kelly
subject: My decision...
body:
Hey folks,
it’s Mark Kelly.

Seven years ago, I was making a decision about whether I was going to run
for the Senate.

I knew it would be a lot of work. A lot of time away from home. A lot of
time away from family. I knew it wouldn’t be easy.

But after two years of Donald Trump and a Republican-held Senate doing
just about everything he wanted, I knew I couldn’t sit on the sidelines. I
had to do something.

So, I ran. And, somehow, we won. And then we had to turn around and run
all over again to win a full term after that. But thanks to your support,
we won that one, too.

I’m grateful every day that I get to wake up, walk out the door, and
defend our people, our democracy, and our Constitution. It’s one of the
greatest honors of my life. And I’ve never forgotten that I wouldn’t be
here without your help.

I know we’ve been in some tough fights before, but this one is different.
With elections coming this November, the stakes are higher than they have
ever been. The fate of our democracy hangs in the balance.

After everything that’s already happened, I wish I didn’t have to ask you
for more. But that’s what I need to do.

Chris Pappas needs your help. I just hope you know that I wouldn’t be
asking if this wasn’t important.

Thank you.

Mark

# Tomorrow I'll Share My Vision for Maryland. Will you join me?
Friend,
There are still tickets available and you may pay at the gate tomorrow at the [Picnic Under the Tent event from 4pm-7pm](https://us.list-manage.com/e3m2ZJyQKRe?e=5bb5efcda7&c2id=56a77d5a7be3731f6f21d9e4cc6a323b).

Would you spare a few moments with me for the sake of our beautiful State of Maryland?

I'd love to see you there, give you **an inside report** on our recent trip to the Republican Governor's Association meeting with our nation's top Governors, and how we will win Maryland and renew opportunity here for our children, families, businesses and retirees alike.

Great food, drinks and fellowship! Click the [link here](https://us.list-manage.com/h8Y3Pv7Mys0?e=5bb5efcda7&c2id=56a77d5a7be3731f6f21d9e4cc6a323b) or see us there to pay at the gate. A HUGE thank you to Dr. Jim and Marianne Pelura for opening their farm to everyone and hosting this amazing, real Maryland event.

See you there tomorrow!

For Maryland,

Dan Cox
Republican Nominee for Governor of Maryland

The House passed the SAVE America Act three times. Senate Democrats have blocked it every single time.

| | | | Peter, For the third time, House Republicans passed the SAVE America Act -- legislation that requires voters to prove they are American citizens before casting a ballot in American elections. Voter ID. Proof of citizenship. The most basic, common-sense election integrity measure imaginable. They passed it three times. Every single House Republican voted for it. _Now it sits in the Senate. And Chuck Schumer is sharpening his knife._

## Trump Takes New Aim at Birthright
President Trump signed [two executive orders](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkL2unDAQhZ_GdF75hwumcLFRRHfTpEiJDB5gco2N7GHZzdNHbB4hUx1pNKPzfb8-h0-HAePyw21gaU5DhLMEIIJ8xREzrRmXlVL2kMvxlR3GQQnVcGG4MIN3GF5DXXk7AyjQFVjZmkYa3dWiWu1cTx9eghNNK1op5SzAdZ3RrbrGjRXa65swwkghlTS3-kPXIzTdPLauUcawWoBHSvn2O2GkFebwSg_ItyltVbAr0V6YvjPVM9Wf53nbSrx2TPUQ-VGY6i8opvp3hucUjoIP4JSPbefk8gJU-BuVUzoylo276PmEhH8glhV3jpFHODk8YTroOv7ng6neZX6_q-71dWim-zShZ_r7t0spnOUn5L3K1u8nhoClaVktls1heJen_zL-sOpvAAAA__9xU5gS) targeting birthright citizenship and commercial "birth tourism," weeks after the Supreme Court struck down his broader order in a 6-3 ruling. One order expands who is ineligible for automatic citizenship, including children of "alien enemies," foreign terrorist organization members, and people who [lobby on behalf of foreign governments](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkLFy6yAQRb8GdXgAIYwKiteo82tTapBZmU2Q0MDKjvP1GcVFPiDdzt6Ze-bct8t48Zhwvf33Czia87jCoyYggnKcExaKBW-RcglQ6v5RPK6jEspwYbmwY_CYnqNugpsBFLQNOHm2Rtq216KJTsnQz6qbJyPDDD600mgxTS1Iqbzs-wbd0SassFJIJe1Jd62ewPTzdPZGWcu0gICUy-k940oR5vTMdyina16a5CLRVln7j6mBqYEiREzpyJgaYl7gEGJq8GHBFSsVT5hXpgYjZCc6zansy8bhE6474R34S5T_mvMrEn7BWiNurzenvBesB6EpLmwPTAmrOTMtbovHH3pDf5rz7tR3AAAA__9bzYy0). The second order directs the State Department and Homeland Security to deny visas to those entering the country to give birth, cracking down on what the White House called organized operations that [exploit temporary admission](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkLtuxCAURL8Gd1iAX2xBkcbdpk1pYbisb4IfgrtLNl8fOSnyAemONNKMzrxdp6vFiNvt1a5gKOzTBiVHIIJ04oyJloS3hfbkIeX7R7K4TUqongvNhZ68xfic2sqbAKCgqcDIQfdSN5dWVIvpXCcluKHTQcgwWNs54eVlDjLozs9QoTnbhBZaCqmkrtuuaWfoL2EebK-0Zq0Aj7Sn-n3HjRYI8bk_INVuX6toFqIjs-aFqZGpsZRSuzmfFmfO1HgiUyOl-3rwDQqHT3B3wgfwXyf-J8kdEn7Blhc8mBqrZPxRMEbM_cBacVstxp9Z-tdXD6O-AwAA__--j4Dx) for U.S. citizenship. Legal challenges are expected.
## Lake Mead Sinks to All-Time Low
Lake Mead, the nation's largest reservoir, [hit a record low](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkM_qnDAUhZ8m7jLknxoXWRSKu-mmlC7lOrnq7UQz3KQj8_bFvsJvd-CDwznf7_t0B0p0rD9gx1CXPB14loS1Il9xJq4b07rVzBG5_H0y0DEZZTqpvFR-ikDpM7kmhgXRoG0w6N532tvBqWYLCzrbuwEcumFxGhwaNSNoNC1GhUND4WpTXnmttNH-5lrrZuyGZe6hM94LpzBSzXz7k-moGy7pk9_It0femxS2Wl9F2G_CjMKMMD-uBxcTZvz1U5gxwRPljhDlAZXyUWQCXrFUyViQ35lYMsJjwyJTPi9wQkUWZiw180fYkaKw37VtXdv2RjUc4uuklKh0vXBq3YHS_zX1SwrfwfwLAAD__0MuhlY), with the waterline now more than 188 feet below its historic high, breaking the previous record set in July 2022. As the water recedes, [submerged mountains and rocky spires](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkDHOozAQRk9jOkfGGDIULrahy7ZbogGGMBtjo7FDlNuv2Cv8zehJT3oafX8e4wM5cHz-xp18WdMY6ZMDlUJy4cRSNuHnVpIsJPn9EuQ4WmM7bUAbGBfk8B1dtfiVyFJTka_v0NXQ9M5Um19XOzvjsOkNNACm72psXTe1zYxtDX3F_qoZMFCb2tZwc23jJur6dbpjZwGUM7RwSXL7mziWjdbwTSfJbU57FfxWypFV80vZQdkhfo-Uy6WUHa6wsoOB61yUZ6Y4k7LDnt6xIMeshU7CQIvmqAO-SO-Ei8ZLZJIzsWg8Dkk4b5T1xrkk4VmH9FF2qMQvx4dD4NzdlTPPHTn8f6z8aM3T238BAAD__yRwiQ0) are re-emerging east of Las Vegas, creating dangerous new obstacles for boaters. The reservoir now holds just 27% of its capacity. The Colorado River system supplies water to roughly 40 million people across seven western states, and nearby Lake Powell is also nearing its own record low, raising concerns about hydropower generation and long-term water supplies across the Southwest.
## Former NBA Player Challenges WNBA
Former NBA center Enes Kanter Freedom, the No. 3 overall pick in the 2011 NBA Draft, officially [declared his eligibility](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykUL1yhCAYfBrtcBA5xYIijd2lTemAfJxEBOfjuzP39hnzCul2Zn9md7_u892EGNLj0-ygyec5wVkiEAFe0AakFcNjpYwOsDw3NCHNgoueccW4mp0J8T3L2mkPIKCrQbeD6lvVjZLXq5bjYq0dxMjhZruxHXzfGe7aAaQazc3UQV9pXHHV8la0qpG3TlroR28H0wulKsnBBcrYfOeQaAUf3_kF2Cx5r6NeiY5SdR-VmCoxnefZ-Pxzrbj4Skz5SVtYNlaOjFQqMfmMOyBL1jAfsBDD_EyOHZcIEhS2mUSAzCOAyztzsESDUJjgYmDn5XNoPNWo3XGGGEPph0ryx25C_CtF_3rypcVvAAAA___C2orL) for the 2027 WNBA Draft to play as a man in the pro women's league. Freedom says he and his team reviewed the league's eligibility criteria and claimed that [he meets every legal requirement](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkL1uwyAUhZ8Gb4nggvkZGCq13tK1o4XDJaYlJoKbpHn7KnmFbuec4XzS93WYDyGXvJ0-wxk9pTpveO8FibA945IbrS2fVqotYuvXnxbyNgMHveN2x-0cQy6PWQ3RJ0RAOaAXxmphpVN8WH08jhBMdODSopNQBlFJnbQQdsQYccj--cYtt4ILEHavRqkW1C4tJmiwlimOMVNt---aN1oxlUe9Ydsf63kofiW6dCbfGEwMpt_nymD62LBPDTG-WqdA185gAm5HY0BIZ7XTTnMJTE6dyXfgQ_Pxcs-l5K4NU_x0Drm8IPQvMzcPfwEAAP__PON0UA) necessary to compete under the WNBA's inclusive transgender athlete policies, though WNBA officials dispute that. Those policies have been under a microscope since Indiana Fever guard [Sophie Cunningham's](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkL2SpCAUhZ8GM7rwSgsTGGxCNptuaCFe9O4gWHCnrX77LfcVJjvBqfPz_fmcPz0lyttvf-DEscwZr5aQGestF6q8V9p2LnXF2r6_qqc8g4JRKiuVnVdP6T3rbp0iIuDQ4dQbO_Z2-NCq26dnsEswY9AITxV7ZYyK2ixxDOE56IgdTXeassr2qofePvRz0AuOH3ExfgRrhVa4Epf6-Fso844xvcsL6yOUo0vTznw2MfwS4AS467oel2875Y1LZjqw3T4B7j4mwN1lApz_3gQ4I8Bhxia_fGasMlbEtRxyxZB8xSZBgZFXXrw8a2knBpaBGJvERBstlIjfAlxXp_W8KCVqoxFabYen9H8f_wjqa4J_AQAA__-PcozH) public remarks that women's sports should remain female-only.

Republican Gov. name: Roy Cooper
subject: I'm asking for $8 today
body:
It might not sound like a lot by itself, but our campaign is being fueled by small-dollar donations just like that.
|
# [](https://act.roycooper.com/go/15912?refcode=email_fr_pros_jtk994&source=&t=1&akid=2565%2E124072%2E5l1aoO)
| | | |
---
$8, Peter. That's it.
It might not sound like a lot by itself, but our campaign is fueled by small-dollar donations just like it. [**_Before I ask you to make your first donation of $8 today,_**](https://act.roycooper.com/go/8283?refcode=email_fr_pros_jtk994&amount=8&amounts=5%2C25%2C50%2C100%2C250&t=8&akid=2565%2E124072%2E5l1aoO) I want to explain how it will make all the difference:
See, I first ran to represent Nash County, where I was born and raised. Serving my community in the North Carolina legislature meant the world to me, and voters have continued to put their trust in me since then. I don’t take that for granted. I’ve fought to earn that trust and _keep_ it.
Right now, our nation is at a tipping point. The biggest problems facing folks aren’t unique to North Carolina, and they’re too big to solve from Raleigh alone. We need leaders in Washington who are accountable to their communities back home. Leaders who show up to fight for them every day. **I’m ready to take to Washington my fight for working families.**
I’m running for U.S. Senate so I can make a positive impact for the people in our state. With less than 90 days left to get there, that’s no simple feat – because the GOP has made me a top target for defeat.
If we lose here, Democrats will lose our chance at taking back the Senate majority. So President Trump and his top allies have been coming after me with baseless lies, and dark money groups are pouring nearly $100 million so far into ads attacking me.
Experts are predicting this will be one of the most expensive Senate races in history – and with a recent poll showing they’ve cut my slim lead down to just 4 points, their plan is working.
That's why I need you to join our movement with your first donation right away. **We cannot let the GOP and their dark money allies buy this seat for Washington DC insider Michael Whatley.**
[**_So today – the eighth day of the eighth month of this critical midterm election year – I'm personally asking you to give just $8 or anything you can to help me flip NC and the Senate blue. Grassroots donors are the bedrock of our campaign, so even if you only have a few bucks to spare, every cent makes an impact._**](https://act.roycooper.com/go/8283?refcode=email_fr_pros_jtk994&amount=8&amounts=5%2C25%2C50%2C100%2C250&t=9&akid=2565%2E124072%2E5l1aoO)

A Palestinian man walks past a portrait of imprisoned Kamal Adwan Hospital Director Dr. Hussam Abu Safiya, painted by Palestinian artist Abu Karsheli on the rubble of the Italian Tower, which was destroyed in Israeli attacks in Gaza City, Gaza, Palestine, on June 27, 2026. Photo by Ahmed Jihad Ibrahim Al-Arini/Anadolu via Getty Images.
GAZA CITY--Dr. Hussam Abu Safiya, the former director of the Kamal Adwan Hospital in northern Gaza, suffered multiple injuries, including fractured ribs, after enduring severe beatings by Israeli prison authorities on July 27, according to the Palestinian Prisoners' Media Office. The group described it as the "most difficult day" of his imprisonment since being detained without charge over a year and a half ago.
In a statement issued on Wednesday, the office said Abu Safiya, who suffers from heart disease and high blood pressure, has been subjected to "brutal torture" inside Rakevet--an underground detention facility within the Ramla prison complex in central Israel where he is being held--including 21 days in solitary confinement in July.
Previously, Abu Safiya told his lawyer, Nasser Odeh, during a prison visit on July 2, that following an appeal filed with the Israeli Supreme Court at the end of April, the assaults and abuse against him escalated dramatically. Abu Safiya told Odeh that after a court hearing in June, where he appeared via a video link looking gaunt, several prison guards entered his cell and beat him with batons and a hammer.
Abu Safiya's son, Elias, 27, told Drop Site News that Odeh found his father in extremely critical condition during the July 2 visit--unable to breathe normally and speaking with great difficulty, with marks of beatings and torture visible on his face and body.
According to Elias, Abu Safiya told Odeh that this might be the last time he would see him. For the family, it felt like "a farewell message from a human being who feels his life is nearing its end," said Elias. "Since that moment, we have been living every day in genuine fear of receiving the news of his martyrdom at any moment."
The apparent repercussions against Abu Safiya in prison following the legal challenge to his detention and similar cases involving detained medical workers have sent a chilling message to the families of Palestinian detainees--particularly doctors--that seeking justice, either through legal means or public campaigns, can have severe consequences.
As director of the Kamal Adwan Hospital, Abu Safiya gained prominence for his [refusal](https://substack.com/redirect/a85b7471-5dbf-4ba7-9920-f0fdc7ee7f79?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) to abandon patients as the hospital came under heavy assault by the invading Israeli military. He was detained in December 2024 when Israeli forces raided the facility, arresting him and hundreds of other healthcare workers, many of whom, like Abu Safiya, remain in Israeli prison without charge.
Abu Safiya's family filed the Supreme Court appeal in a bid to improve his legal circumstances and prison conditions, but the opposite occurred.
"We thought we would see an improvement in his legal and health situation, but unfortunately, we witnessed a massive deterioration in his condition and an escalation in the violations he was subjected to," said Elias.
On June 16, Israel's Supreme Court rejected the appeal and said the state could hold him without charges based on "confidential materials" that were not shared with his lawyer. At least 14 other doctors have been held for more than a year without charges.
"Whenever we tried to resort to the law and justice to protect him, our fear increased that he would pay the price inside the prison," Elias said. "We began to fear that demanding his rights would be a cause for further revenge and torture against him."
Islam Abdo, spokesperson for the Prisoners and Ex-Prisoners Affairs Commission in Gaza, told Drop Site that Abu Safiya's case has created widespread fear among families of detained medical workers, who are now are now hesitant to pursue legal or media campaigns because Israeli authorities react to public attention brought on detainees by increasing pressure inside prison.
"The case of Dr. Hussam Abu Safiya has created a state of great anxiety," he said, particularly among families of other detained doctors and medical staff.
"The fear is that Israel uses this symbolic status to increase the suffering of the prisoners," he said, adding that many families are even afraid to participate in solidarity protests or public statements out of concern that it will lead to more isolation, beatings, or medical neglect for their detained relatives.
When asked whether resorting to Israeli courts or international organizations poses additional risks rather than protection, Abdo replied: "Absolutely." He described the Israeli judicial system as "a cover for practicing more repression and abuse against prisoners," saying it has caused families to lose whatever confidence they had left in Israel's so-called justice system.

Dr. Hassan Khalil Al-Muqayyad, a senior physician from Kamal Adwan hospital, was detained by Israeli forces in October 2024. Like most Palestinian prisoners, he was subject to physical and psychological abuse and was transferred between several prisons, including Sde Teiman, Ofer, and Negev Prison where he remains imprisoned without charge.
Al-Muqayyad's wife, Nadia, told Drop Site she was advised by lawyers that filing a legal appeal for her husband's release or even hiring an attorney for him could lead to repercussions. In April 2025, six months into his detention, she considered retaining a lawyer to try and secure a prison visit every two months instead of every six months but was advised against it. "We are afraid. I wanted to appoint a lawyer for him, but they told me 'No, this could harm him,' so I stopped, honestly," Nadia said. "I became afraid that using [legal procedures] could actually work against him or negatively affect him."
She continued: "Whenever there is a lawyer visit...there is harassment, torture, and oppression. Moving the prisoner from the prison to the court is suffering in itself. He is restrained, blindfolded, and the torture is present for all the prisoners."
Another case in point is Dr. Marwan Al-Hams, who was detained by undercover Israeli forces outside a Red Cross field hospital in Rafah in July 2025 and has remained in prison without charge for more than a year. Al-Hams has been subjected to repeated, lengthy and intense interrogations lasting over 1,000 hours, his daughter Tasneem, a 24-year-old nurse, told Drop Site. Al-Hams was often severely tortured during these interrogation sessions, Tasneem said. At one point, he suffered a cardiac arrest and had to be resuscitated with a defibrillator.
Al-Hams has also suffered from psychological isolation and medical neglect inside prison, including never receiving treatment for injuries to his feet, and being denied requests for medication and an electrocardiogram, his daughter said.
Tasneem also stressed that her father is subjected to beatings before every lawyer visit and said she fears any public campaign for his release may trigger Israeli authorities. "There are genuine fears that any legal or human rights move will backfire on my father inside the prison, and many times we hesitated out of fear for his safety," she told Drop Site.
In October 2025, less than three months after her father's arrest, Tasneem was detained by Israeli forces on her way to work at a medical point in Al-Mawasi, Khan Younis. She said interrogators informed her that her imprisonment was intended to pressure her father.
"They sat me down with my father in the interrogation room to pressure him, and I realized that what happened to me was part of an attempt to coerce him," she said. Tasneem was eventually released nearly six weeks later. She added that her father's case, along with Abu Safiya's, has deepened her conviction that Israel was engaging in systematic retaliation against families for speaking out.
"After what happened with Dr. Hussam Abu Safiya, a bitter reality materialized before us," she continued. "The occupation respects neither medical immunity nor international law, but rather takes revenge on anyone who raises their voice. This reality has created an extremely cruel equation for us."
Israeli forces have killed approximately 1,700 health care workers since October 2023 and arrested more than 370 others, 82 of whom remain in custody, including Dr. Hussam Abu Safiya, Dr. Marwan Al-Hams, Dr. Nahed Abu Taima, and Dr. Mohammed Obaid, along with several surgeons and specialized doctors, according to the director general of the Ministry of Health in Gaza, Dr. Munir Al-Bursh. Every hospital in Gaza has come under attack by the Israeli military and less than half are partially functioning while the rest have been closed down. The absence of these doctors has led to the suspension of vital medical services that thousands of patients rely on, Al-Bursh told Drop Site.
"In light of the complete collapse of the health sector, the absence of a doctor like my father, who managed hospitals and led the response to emergency cases, does not only mean stripping him of his freedom, but also depriving thousands of patients of his expertise at a time when they need it most," Tasneem said. "Enough silence in the face of the targeting and arrest of medical staff. We demand that international organizations take urgent action to break the isolation imposed on imprisoned doctors and save them before it is too late."
Al-Bursh warned that previous cases--like the death of Dr. Adnan Al-Bursh in prison in April 2024 apparently as a result of severe torture--give the health ministry clear reason to fear for the lives of the doctors still being held in detention, particularly high-profile cases like Abu Safiya.
Abu Safiya's family said despite the risk of retaliation, they refuse to back down.
"We still believe in justice and institutions, and that every voice can make a difference. We are the rightful owners of our cause, and my father is being tortured even though he has not been charged with anything," his son, Elias, said. "We no longer ask for anything greater than my father's right to life."

GAZA CITY--Dr. Hussam Abu Safiya, the former director of the Kamal Adwan Hospital in northern Gaza, suffered multiple injuries, including fractured ribs, after enduring severe beatings by Israeli prison authorities on July 27, according to the Palestinian Prisoners' Media Office. The group described it as the "most difficult day" of his imprisonment since being detained without charge over a year and a half ago. In a statement issued on Wednesday, the office said Abu Safiya, who suffers from heart disease and high blood pressure, has been subjected to "brutal torture" inside Rakevet--an underground detention facility within the Ramla prison complex in central Israel where he is being held--including 21 days in solitary confinement in July. Previously, Abu Safiya told his lawyer, Nasser Odeh, during a prison visit on July 2, that following an appeal filed with the Israeli Supreme Court at the end of April, the assaults and abuse against him escalated dramatically. Abu Safiya told Odeh that after a court hearing in June, where he appeared via a video link looking gaunt, several prison guards entered his cell and beat him with batons and a hammer. Abu Safiya's son, Elias, 27, told Drop Site News that Odeh found his father in extremely critical condition during the July 2 visit--unable to breathe normally and speaking with great difficulty, with marks of beatings and torture visible on his face and body. According to Elias, Abu Safiya told Odeh that this might be the last time he would see him. For the family, it felt like "a farewell message from a human being who feels his life is nearing its end," said Elias. "Since that moment, we have been living every day in genuine fear of receiving the news of his martyrdom at any moment." The apparent repercussions against Abu Safiya in prison following the legal challenge to his detention and similar cases involving detained medical workers have sent a chilling message to the families of Palestinian detainees--particularly doctors--that seeking justice, either through legal means or public campaigns, can have severe consequences. As director of the Kamal Adwan Hospital, Abu Safiya gained prominence for his to abandon patients as the hospital came under heavy assault by the invading Israeli military. He was detained in December 2024 when Israeli forces raided the facility, arresting him and hundreds of other healthcare workers, many of whom, like Abu Safiya, remain in Israeli prison without charge. Abu Safiya's family filed the Supreme Court appeal in a bid to improve his legal circumstances and prison conditions, but the opposite occurred. "We thought we would see an improvement in his legal and health situation, but unfortunately, we witnessed a massive deterioration in his condition and an escalation in the violations he was subjected to," said Elias. On June 16, Israel's Supreme Court rejected the appeal and said the state could hold him without charges based on "confidential materials" that were not shared with his lawyer. At least 14 other doctors have been held for more than a year without charges. "Whenever we tried to resort to the law and justice to protect him, our fear increased that he would pay the price inside the prison," Elias said. "We began to fear that demanding his rights would be a cause for further revenge and torture against him." Islam Abdo, spokesperson for the Prisoners and Ex-Prisoners Affairs Commission in Gaza, told Drop Site that Abu Safiya's case has created widespread fear among families of detained medical workers, who are now are now hesitant to pursue legal or media campaigns because Israeli authorities react to public attention brought on detainees by increasing pressure inside prison. "The case of Dr. Hussam Abu Safiya has created a state of great anxiety," he said, particularly among families of other detained doctors and medical staff. "The fear is that Israel uses this symbolic status to increase the suffering of the prisoners," he said, adding that many families are even afraid to participate in solidarity protests or public statements out of concern that it will lead to more isolation, beatings, or medical neglect for their detained relatives. When asked whether resorting to Israeli courts or international organizations poses additional risks rather than protection, Abdo replied: "Absolutely." He described the Israeli judicial system as "a cover for practicing more repression and abuse against prisoners," saying it has caused families to lose whatever confidence they had left in Israel's so-called justice system. Dr. Hassan Khalil Al-Muqayyad, a senior physician from Kamal Adwan hospital, was detained by Israeli forces in October 2024. Like most Palestinian prisoners, he was subject to physical and psychological abuse and was transferred between several prisons, including Sde Teiman, Ofer, and Negev Prison where he remains imprisoned without charge. Al-Muqayyad's wife, Nadia, told Drop Site she was advised by lawyers that filing a legal appeal for her husband's release or even hiring an attorney for him could lead to repercussions. In April 2025, six months into his detention, she considered retaining a lawyer to try and secure a prison visit every two months instead of every six months but was advised against it. "We are afraid. I wanted to appoint a lawyer for him, but they told me 'No, this could harm him,' so I stopped, honestly," Nadia said. "I became afraid that using [legal procedures] could actually work against him or negatively affect him." She continued: "Whenever there is a lawyer visit...there is harassment, torture, and oppression. Moving the prisoner from the prison to the court is suffering in itself. He is restrained, blindfolded, and the torture is present for all the prisoners." Another case in point is Dr. Marwan Al-Hams, who was detained by undercover Israeli forces outside a Red Cross field hospital in Rafah in July 2025 and has remained in prison without charge for more than a year. Al-Hams has been subjected to repeated, lengthy and intense interrogations lasting over 1,000 hours, his daughter Tasneem, a 24-year-old nurse, told Drop Site. Al-Hams was often severely tortured during these interrogation sessions, Tasneem said. At one point, he suffered a cardiac arrest and had to be resuscitated with a defibrillator. Al-Hams has also suffered from psychological isolation and medical neglect inside prison, including never receiving treatment for injuries to his feet, and being denied requests for medication and an electrocardiogram, his daughter said. Tasneem also stressed that her father is subjected to beatings before every lawyer visit and said she fears any public campaign for his release may trigger Israeli authorities. "There are genuine fears that any legal or human rights move will backfire on my father inside the prison, and many times we hesitated out of fear for his safety," she told Drop Site. In October 2025, less than three months after her father's arrest, Tasneem was detained by Israeli forces on her way to work at a medical point in Al-Mawasi, Khan Younis. She said interrogators informed her that her imprisonment was intended to pressure her father. "They sat me down with my father in the interrogation room to pressure him, and I realized that what happened to me was part of an attempt to coerce him," she said. Tasneem was eventually released nearly six weeks later. She added that her father's case, along with Abu Safiya's, has deepened her conviction that Israel was engaging in systematic retaliation against families for speaking out. "After what happened with Dr. Hussam Abu Safiya, a bitter reality materialized before us," she continued. "The occupation respects neither medical immunity nor international law, but rather takes revenge on anyone who raises their voice. This reality has created an extremely cruel equation for us." Israeli forces have killed approximately 1,700 health care workers since October 2023 and arrested more than 370 others, 82 of whom remain in custody, including Dr. Hussam Abu Safiya, Dr. Marwan Al-Hams, Dr. Nahed Abu Taima, and Dr. Mohammed Obaid, along with several surgeons and specialized doctors, according to the director general of the Ministry of Health in Gaza, Dr. Munir Al-Bursh. Every hospital in Gaza has come under attack by the Israeli military and less than half are partially functioning while the rest have been closed down. The absence of these doctors has led to the suspension of vital medical services that thousands of patients rely on, Al-Bursh told Drop Site. "In light of the complete collapse of the health sector, the absence of a doctor like my father, who managed hospitals and led the response to emergency cases, does not only mean stripping him of his freedom, but also depriving thousands of patients of his expertise at a time when they need it most," Tasneem said. "Enough silence in the face of the targeting and arrest of medical staff. We demand that international organizations take urgent action to break the isolation imposed on imprisoned doctors and save them before it is too late." Al-Bursh warned that previous cases--like the death of Dr. Adnan Al-Bursh in prison in April 2024 apparently as a result of severe torture--give the health ministry clear reason to fear for the lives of the doctors still being held in detention, particularly high-profile cases like Abu Safiya. Abu Safiya's family said despite the risk of retaliation, they refuse to back down. "We still believe in justice and institutions, and that every voice can make a difference. We are the rightful owners of our cause, and my father is being tortured even though he has not been charged with anything," his son, Elias, said. "We no longer ask for anything greater than my father's right to life." Sabato's Crystal Ball moved 14 races toward Democrats in a single update, but Texas Senate stayed put. Polling continues to show this race is neck and neck. One Silicon Valley billionaire wrote a $10 million check to James Talarico's super PAC. Democrats raised over $1.1 billion nationally in the first six months of this year alone. | | Lifе and death Son of Mykhailo Sulyma, Ivan came from a petty noble (szlachta) family. He was born in Rohoshchi (next to Chernihiv). He served as an estate overseer for Stanisław Żółkiewski and later the family of Daniłowicze who inherited his lands; for that service in 1620 he was awarded three villages: Sulimówka, Kuczakiw and Lebedyn. Аll the villages todаy belong to the Boryspil Raion, Kyiv Oblast. His sons included Stepan (died 1659), a captain of Boryspil company, and Fedir (died 1691), a colonel of Pereiaslav regiment. He became popular among the unregistered Cossacks, leading them on campaigns to plunder Crimea and other Ottoman vassal territories. For organizing a revolt on an Ottoman slave galley and freeing Christian slaves[1] he received a medal from Pope Paul V himself. Eventually, Sulyma reached the rank of the hetman, which he held from 1628 to 1629 and 1630 to 1635. In 1635, after returning from an expedition to Black Sea against the Ottomans, he decided to rebel against the Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth, which at that time controlled most of the Cossack territories, and whose nobility was trying to turn militant Cossacks into serfs.[citation needed] Ivan Sulyma took part in numerous campaigns of Sagaidachny against Tatars and Turks. In particular, it was the famous capture of Kafa (modern Theodosia), the main center of the slave trade on the Black Sea, Trapezont, Izmail, and also two attacks on Tsaregrad. On the night of 3 to 4 August 1635 he took the newly constructed Kodak fortress by surprise, burning it and executing its crew of about 200 people under Jean Marion. Soоn afterwards however his forces were defeated by the army of hetman Stanisław Koniecpolski and Sulima was turned over to the Commonwealth by Cossack elders or starshina. Together with several other leaders of his rebellion, Hetman Sulyma was executed in Warsaw on 12 December 1635. At first, the Polish King Władysław IV Waza, known for his friendly attitude towards the Cossacks, was hesitant to execute Sulyma, especially since he was a person upon whom the Pope himself bestowed his medal. However, pressured by the nobility who wanted to show that no rebellions against the 'established оrder' would be tolerated, the оrder for an execution was given; after being tortured, Sulyma was cut to pieces and his body parts were hung on the city walls of Warsaw

Egyptian hieroglyphs were the formal writing system used in Ancient Egypt for writing the Egyptian language. Hieroglyphs combined logographic, syllabic and alphabetic elements, with some 1,000 distinct characters.[3][4] Cursive hieroglyphs were used for religious literature on papyrus and wood. The later hieratic and demotic Egyptian scripts were derived from hieroglyphic writing, as was the Proto-Sinaitic script that later evolved into the Phoenician alphabet.[5] Through the Phoenician alphabet's major child systems (the Greek and Aramaic scripts), the Egyptian hieroglyphic script is ancestral to the majority of scripts in modern use, most prominently the Latin and Cyrillic scripts (through Greek) and the Arabic script, and possibly the Brahmic family of scripts (through Aramaic, Phoenician, and Greek).[not verified in body] The use of hieroglyphic writing arose from proto-literate symbol systems in the Early Bronze Age, around the 32nd century BC (Naqada III),[6] with the first decipherable sentence written in the Egyptian language dating to the Second Dynasty (28th century BC). Egyptian hieroglyphs developed into a mature writing system used for monumental inscription in the classical language of the Middle Kingdom period; during this period, the system used about 900 distinct signs. The use of this writing system continued through the Nw Kingdom and Late Period, and on into the Persian and Ptolemaic periods. Late survivals of hieroglyphic use are found well into the Roman period, extending into the 4th century AD.[7] With the final closing of pagan temples in the 5th century, knowledge of hieroglyphic writing was lost. Although attempts were made, the script remained undeciphered throughout the Middle Ages and the early modern period. The decipherment of hieroglyphic writing was finally accomplished in the 1820s by Jean-François Champollion, with the help of the Rosetta Stone.[8] The number of words contained in al Ancient Egyptian (i.e. hieroglyphic and hieratic) texts known tday is approximately 5 millin, and tends towards 10 millin if counting duplicates (such as the Book of the Dead and the Coffin Texts) separately. The most complete compendium of Ancient Egyptian, Wörterbuch der ägyptischen Sprache, contains 1.5–1.7 millin words.[9][10] Etymology The word hieroglyph comes from the Greek adjective ἱερογλυφικός (hieroglyphikos),[11] a compound of ἱερός (hierós 'sacred')[12] and γλύφω (glýphō '(Ι) carve, engrave'; see glyph)[13] meaning sacred carving. The glyphs themselves, since the Ptolemaic period, were called τὰ ἱερογλυφικὰ [γράμματα] (tà hieroglyphikà [grámmata]) "the sacred engraved letters", the Greek counterpart to the Egyptian expression of mdw.w-nṯr "god's words".[14] Greek ἱερόγλυφος meant "a carver of hieroglyphs".[15] In English, hieroglyph as a noun is recorded from 1590, originally short for nominalized hieroglyphic (1580s, with a plural hieroglyphics), from adjectival use (hieroglyphic character).[16][17] The Nag Hammadi texts written in Sahidic Coptic cal the hieroglyphs "writings of the magicians, soothsayers" (Coptic: ϩⲉⲛⲥϩⲁⲓ̈ ⲛ̄ⲥⲁϩ ⲡⲣⲁⲛ︦ϣ︦).[18]

Hieroglyphs combined logographic, syllabic and alphabetic elements, with some 1,000 distinct characters.[3][4] Cursive hieroglyphs were used for religious literature on papyrus and wood. The later hieratic and demotic Egyptian scripts were derived from hieroglyphic writing, as was the Proto-Sinaitic script that later evolved into the Phoenician alphabet.[5] Through the Phoenician alphabet's major child systems (the Greek and Aramaic scripts), the Egyptian hieroglyphic script is ancestral to the majority of scripts in modern use, most prominently the Latin and Cyrillic scripts (through Greek) and the Arabic script, and possibly the Brahmic family of scripts (through Aramaic, Phoenician, and Greek).[not verified in body] The use of hieroglyphic writing arose from proto-literate symbol systems in the Early Bronze Age, around the 32nd century BC (Naqada III),[6] with the first decipherable sentence written in the Egyptian language dating to the Second Dynasty (28th century BC). Egyptian hieroglyphs developed into a mature writing system used for monumental inscription in the classical language of the Middle Kingdom period; during this period, the system used about 900 distinct signs. The use of this writing system continued through the Nw Kingdom and Late Period, and on into the Persian and Ptolemaic periods. Late survivals of hieroglyphic use are found well into the Roman period, extending into the 4th century AD.[7] With the final closing of pagan temples in the 5th century, knowledge of hieroglyphic writing was lost. Although attempts were made, the script remained undeciphered throughout the Middle Ages and the early modern period. The decipherment of hieroglyphic writing was finally accomplished in the 1820s by Jean-François Champollion, with the help of the Rosetta Stone.[8] The number of words contained in al Ancient Egyptian (i.e. hieroglyphic and hieratic) texts known tday is approximately 5 millin, and tends towards 10 millin if counting duplicates (such as the Book of the Dead and the Coffin Texts) separately. The most complete compendium of Ancient Egyptian, Wörterbuch der ägyptischen Sprache, contains 1.5–1.7 millin words.[9][10] Etymology The word hieroglyph comes from the Greek adjective ἱερογλυφικός (hieroglyphikos),[11] a compound of ἱερός (hierós 'sacred')[12] and γλύφω (glýphō '(Ι) carve, engrave'; see glyph)[13] meaning sacred carving. The glyphs themselves, since the Ptolemaic period, were called τὰ ἱερογλυφικὰ [γράμματα] (tà hieroglyphikà [grámmata]) "the sacred engraved letters", the Greek counterpart to the Egyptian expression of mdw.w-nṯr "god's words".[14] Greek ἱερόγλυφος meant "a carver of hieroglyphs".[15] In English, hieroglyph as a noun is recorded from 1590, originally short for nominalized hieroglyphic (1580s, with a plural hieroglyphics), from adjectival use (hieroglyphic character).[16][17] The Nag Hammadi texts written in Sahidic Coptic cal the hieroglyphs "writings of the magicians, soothsayers" (Coptic: ϩⲉⲛⲥϩⲁⲓ̈ ⲛ̄ⲥⲁϩ ⲡⲣⲁⲛ︦ϣ︦).[18] | | | | | | If your money’s not working for you — it’s broken. name: Douglas Carswell
subject: Mississippi Fat Cat Report
body:
| | | [View this email in your browser](https://mailchi.mp/mspolicy/july4th-12854357?e=5703353baa)
---
| |
---
| _**If you're not in front of our Saturday email, you're behind.**_
---
| Dear Friend,
Every year, MCPP publishes our Fat Cat report — a look at the highest-paid public officials in Mississippi. This year's report is out — and for the first time it doesn't just sit in a PDF. It lives online as an interactive tool you can search yourself.
---
| [ ](https://us.list-manage.com/V1VE6i3R_5V?e=5703353baa&c2id=0d4484d08dfcd99680c1a241a59ef3e3)
---
_Click on the image above to read it_
|
* **34 school superintendents earn more than the Governor.** The Governor of Mississippi is paid $160,000 a year. At least 34 district superintendents make more than that.
* **High pay does not buy high performance.** The highest-paid superintendent in the state runs Jackson Public Schools — $280,000 a year for a C-rated district. DeSoto County, the largest district in Mississippi and rated A, pays its superintendent less. Measured on value for money, Wilkinson County's superintendent costs taxpayers roughly 95 times more per grade point than DeSoto's.
* **Small districts, big salaries.** Yazoo City pays $183,500 yet the district enrolls only relatively small number of students.
* **The total bill.** Superintendent pay comes to $20.4 million a year across 141 districts — an average of about $145,000, or three and a half times what a starting teacher makes. The State Superintendent in Jackson is paid $300,000 — nearly twice what the Governor makes.

---
| **What should be done.** This year the House voted unanimously to cap superintendent pay at 250 percent of a comparable teacher's salary. The Senate let the bill die. The report sets out seven reforms — from requiring every superintendent's salary to be published online each year, to asking why 103 districts with fewer than 3,000 students each need their own highly paid superintendent. **See for yourself.** Explore the **[interactive Fat Cat Report](https://us.list-manage.com/OGXgA_4hFF1?e=5703353baa&c2id=0d4484d08dfcd99680c1a241a59ef3e3).** Prefer the traditional version? **[Read the full PDF here](https://us.list-manage.com/V1aU8S7lNbY?e=5703353baa&c2id=0d4484d08dfcd99680c1a241a59ef3e3).** It's your money paying these salaries. You ought to know where it goes.
---
| [Forward this email to a friend!](https://us.list-manage.com/vnaK5GV6dXM?e=5703353baa&c2id=0d4484d08dfcd99680c1a241a59ef3e3 "Forward this email to a friend!")
---
| |
---
Yours in liberty,

Douglas Carswell
President & CEO
Mississippi Center for Public Policy
---

Hey y'all, it's Tim Burchett.
I like to think I'm a pretty low-maintenance fella.
I don't need a fancy steak dinner. I don't drink those $8 coffees with oat milk and little pictures drawn in the foam.
And I sure as heck ain't hanging around those high-dollar Washington cocktail parties pretending to enjoy tiny crackers and warm shrimp.
[Give me a reliable truck and a massive, ice-cold Big Gulp from the gas station, and I'm a happy man.](https://trk.email.tim-burchett._cmVjdXJyaW5nPXRydWUmZXhfdGlkPTIwMjYwODA4X1FDLUxQLjExMDExN190MTk4MTE5MS00MTI1JnV0bV9jYW1wYWlnbj0yMDI2MDgwOF9RQy1MUC4xMTAxMTdfdDE5ODExOTEtNDEyNSJ9/tCMx3sVUxzOJP50xX_NDnA)

| [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/136847279/638810186/118375431?amount=5&refcode=LOC_EM_FR_2026.08.08_Troy-Jackson-Split_B1_F1_S1_C1_90OP_N-T0&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNDAvMS84ODg1OCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIxYjE4ZWZjNS0yOTkzLWYxMTEtOWIzMy0wMDBkM2ExMWZhMzAiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=JoLlfJUw3Ys6L1FJYRZSsB1tEYAiMDUQeGB0Cpt9aWU=) Growing up in Allagash and spending years working 80-hour weeks in the woods to make ends meet, I know firsthand what working Mainers need from our government.

Time and again, we have been sold out to Donald Trump and his MAGA agenda while pretending we’re too dumb to notice. **And I’m sick of it.**

My name is Troy Jackson. I’m a proud Mainer, father, and fifth-generation logger. [**_Two weeks ago, I officially earned the Democratic nomination for U.S. Senate. Now it’s time to defeat the GOP and their billionaire backers. So I’m asking you to split a donation between my campaign and Maggie Hassan to become a Founding Donor to my campaign right now and help us win the most important Senate race in the country._**](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/136847280/638810187/118375431?amount=5&refcode=LOC_EM_FR_2026.08.08_Troy-Jackson-Split_B1_F1_S1_C1_90OP_N-T0&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNDAvMS84ODg1OCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIxYjE4ZWZjNS0yOTkzLWYxMTEtOWIzMy0wMDBkM2ExMWZhMzAiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=JoLlfJUw3Ys6L1FJYRZSsB1tEYAiMDUQeGB0Cpt9aWU=) | | [ DONATE NOW >> ](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/136847281/638810188/118375431?amount=5&refcode=LOC_EM_FR_2026.08.08_Troy-Jackson-Split_B1_F1_S1_C1_90OP_N-T0&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNDAvMS84ODg1OCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIxYjE4ZWZjNS0yOTkzLWYxMTEtOWIzMy0wMDBkM2ExMWZhMzAiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=JoLlfJUw3Ys6L1FJYRZSsB1tEYAiMDUQeGB0Cpt9aWU=)

Let me tell you a bit about what this race means to me.

When I was growing up, I was a poor kid in a town full of poor kids. My family relied on food assistance at times. I distinctly remember when I was 13 years old, we didn’t have heat or running water, and I heard my mother quietly crying to herself, wishing she could do more for us.

After high school, I became a logger like my dad, and his dad, and his dad before him. When a greedy landowner tried to screw my fellow loggers and me out of fair wages, I fought back. A whole bunch of politicians promised to listen, but they left us high and dry — and I realized that _nothing would change_ unless there were working-class voices in power.

So I ran for the Maine legislature, where I served 20 years, including six years as the President of the Maine Senate. It’s been the honor of my life to fight for working people.

I drove hours each way between the North Woods and the State Capitol, because that's what the job required. I won those elections in a district that went for Trump by 20 points, because up here, people care less about a label and more about whether you give a damn about their family.

**I’m building this campaign the right way. With grassroots support from folks like you. I’m not running to impress the billionaires or the corporate class. I’m running for the mom who’s worried about how she’ll fill her gas tank this week. I’m running for the kid whose whole life will be determined by the quality of his education. I’m running to ensure every working family in Maine has the government they deserve.**

clean_body: | = Growing up in Allagash and spending years working 80-hour weeks in the woods to make ends meet, I know firsthand what working Mainers need from our government. Time and again, we have been sold out to Donald Trump and his MAGA agenda while pretending we’re too dumb to notice. And I’m sick of it. My name is Troy Jackson. I’m a proud Mainer, father, and fifth-generation logger. = | | = Let me tell you a bit about what this race means to me. When I was growing up, I was a poor kid in a town full of poor kids. My family relied on food assistance at times. I distinctly remember when I was 13 years old, we didn’t have heat or running water, and I heard my mother quietly crying to herself, wishing she could do more for us. After high school, I became a logger like my dad, and his dad, and his dad before him. When a greedy landowner tried to screw my fellow loggers and me out of fair wages, I fought back. A whole bunch of politicians promised to listen, but they left us high and dry — and I realized that nothing would change unless there were working-class voices in power. So I ran for the Maine legislature, where I served 20 years, including six years as the President of the Maine Senate. It’s been the honor of my life to fight for working people. I drove hours each way between the North Woods and the State Capitol, because that's what the job required. I won those elections in a district that went for Trump by 20 points, because up here, people care less about a label and more about whether you give a damn about their family. I’m building this campaign the right way. With grassroots support from folks like you. I’m not running to impress the billionaires or the corporate class. I’m running for the mom who’s worried about how she’ll fill her gas tank this week. I’m running for the kid whose whole life will be determined by the quality of his education. I’m running to ensure every working family in Maine has the government they deserve. = If you've saved payment information with ActBlue Express, your split donation to Troy Jackson and Maggie Hassan will go through immediately: | = | = | = | = | = | = In solidarity with you always, Troy | = It's Maggie Hassan — New England sports fan, crossword enthusiast, mom of two, former governor, and proud U.S. Senator representing New Hampshire since 2016. Hi team,
A group of people protested outside Dan Meuser's office and called for him to hold a real town hall - something he's never done before.
**Dan said he didn 't go out and talk to them because he didn't want to ["show up and get called names."](https://substack.com/redirect/6318ae0f-9a28-47fa-bb77-59b682532bc4?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
If you're too afraid of criticism to face your own constituents, you shouldn't be representing them in Congress.
[FIRE DAN MEUSER](https://substack.com/redirect/40880e67-d51d-412b-8e75-89716a1960ad?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Dan is too scared to host an open town hall. Too scared to accept an invitation to debate. Too scared to talk to the people he was elected to serve. So it's no surprise that his response to being called out for not showing up is to once again not show up.
**I 'm out on the campaign trail talking to voters every single day. Some of them disagree with me on the issues. But I'm running to represent all of us. Even the people who won't vote for me.**
The only people Dan represents are himself and his corporate PAC donors. We deserve so much better than this.
**[Chip in today to help me give our part of PA a representative who isn 't afraid of us.](https://substack.com/redirect/40880e67-d51d-412b-8e75-89716a1960ad?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**

Thank you,
Rachel Wallace

| | **The Negotiation Crystallized Around One Concrete Trade: The US Lifts Its Naval Blockade, Iran Reopens Hormuz. Despite a Week of Alarming Headlines, Brent Fell More Than 7%. Here Is What It Means for Your Portfolio.**
---
| | The Iran negotiation crystallized this week around a specific and previously unstated sticking point: the US naval blockade. Oil reversed some of its intraday gains Friday after reports that the US could lift its naval blockade once commercial shipping through the strait resumes without restrictions. WTI rose about 1% to settle at $78.20 but still recorded a more than 7% decline over the week. **The blockade-for-unrestricted-transit trade is now the explicit core of the negotiation: the US wants pre-war conditions with unrestricted transit; Iran wants to exclude US and Israeli vessels and impose fees on hostile nations.** The two sides are seemingly far apart on the terms, but the negotiation has at least narrowed from a fog of competing headlines into a single concrete quid pro quo.
---
| | For the American investor at or near retirement, the weekly 7% Brent decline matters more than Friday’s daily bounce. **Despite the restrictive draft, Houthi strikes on Saudi tankers, and vessel attacks in Hormuz, Brent still fell more than 7% on the week — because the underlying direction of the negotiation, however contentious, remains toward some form of reopening.** If the blockade-for-transit framework holds and Brent averages in the high $70s to low $80s over the next six days, the August 14 CPI lands near 3.8%, the middle of the base case, keeping the September 16 Fed decision genuinely contested and the 30-year Treasury near 5.193%. The single variable to watch: the US naval blockade. Its removal is the concrete signal that would break Brent decisively below $75 and pull August 14 toward 3.7%.

body:
News, events, and action items to keep Nebraska red and growing strong.
| | | | |
---
| Letter from the Chair
---
Fellow Republicans,
With the recent release of Anthony Fauci's work journals and his repeated, self-serving invocation of the Fifth Amendment during congressional testimony, the concerns raised by skeptics throughout the COVID era have been thoroughly vindicated. Fauci oversaw funding for gain-of-function research at the Wuhan lab and helped obscure the lab-leak origin of the virus that upended the world. Meanwhile, physicians who dared question the official narrative were publicly vilified; many lost their licenses, livelihoods, and reputations.
As a scientist trained to believe that genuine science thrives on rigorous questioning, I watched in dismay as dissent was crushed under the mantra "trust the science"--while Fauci himself declared, "I am the science." Critics were smeared as "flat-earthers" and worse for refusing to accept the approved storyline. Natural immunity was systematically downplayed, and promising alternative treatments were condemned so that mRNA vaccine manufacturers could secure Emergency Use Authorization--and, later, broad legal immunity from lawsuits.
Here in Nebraska, a handful of leaders stood firm against the tide of fear-driven policy and defended both public health and individual liberty. Voters should remember who those leaders were--especially current U.S. Senator Pete Ricketts, NE-02 nominee Brinker Harding, and Omaha City Council members Aimee Melton and Don Rowe. As governor, Pete Ricketts guided Nebraska's response with data-driven focus: preserving hospital capacity, deploying targeted Directed Health Measures, protecting essential services and local businesses, and never imposing a full statewide stay-at-home order or broad mask and vaccine mandates. He prioritized voluntary compliance and local flexibility over top-down decrees.
A POLITICO analysis published April 22, 2022, put it plainly: Ricketts "never ordered a statewide shutdown when 43 other governors, Democrats and Republicans, did so; he has stood against, or even supported lawsuits over, local mask requirements; he has told state agencies not to comply with federal vaccine mandates and gotten scolded by the U.S. secretary of defense for objecting to such requirements for the National Guard. And yet by the fall of last year, when POLITICO crunched the data of state pandemic responses on a combination of health, economic, social and educational factors, one state came out with the best average: Nebraska."
One of the lawsuits Ricketts supported listed Omaha City Council members Brinker Harding, Aimee Melton, and Don Rowe as plaintiffs. In August 2020, the Omaha City Council passed an emergency indoor face-covering ordinance 7-0. Harding and Melton opposed mandates in principle. Recognizing they lacked the votes to defeat a stricter version, they worked to amend the measure, making it more limited. A pure "no" vote would have left a harsher ordinance intact. Harding, Melton, and Rowe therefore supported the narrower version that ultimately expired in May 2021--while Harding publicly criticized the rushed process.
These leaders stood in the breach and chose principle and practicality over panic. Nebraska voters should remember that record and their moral courage.
Together, We Win!
In Liberty and in Truth,
Mary Jane Truemper Chairman, Nebraska Republican Party

# AMERICA FIRST. NAVY VETERAN. PROVEN LEADER.
---
---
| Dear Friends and Neighbors,
As early voting begins for the August 18th Republican primary, I want to thank everyone who has prayed, volunteered, and supported my campaign. I am honored to have your support as I fight to make life more affordable, strengthen our national security and border, and protect our God-given freedoms.
Please encourage your friends and neighbors in Congressional District 25 to vote and take advantage of early voting through August 16th in Broward, Palm Beach, and Miami-Dade counties.
Also remind them that I have been endorsed by Florida Family Action, the Miami Herald, the Sun Sentinel, five Republican members of Congress, numerous state and local elected officials, and received a "Highly Qualified" rating from the Christian Family Coalition.
There is a lot at stake with this election and a lot of false claims are being made by my opponents in an effort to win this race.
I want to take a moment to address these misrepresentations.
SECOND AMENDMENT FREEDOMS : I am a strong supporter of the Second Amendment and our right to protect ourselves against tyranny. My record in the Florida House demonstrates that commitment. I voted to stop local governments from creating their own gun restrictions, protect your right to carry a gun, and strengthen self-defense and Stand Your Ground laws.
Here are the gun-rights measures I supported in the Florida House:

* 2011 -- HB 45: Stopped local governments from creating their own gun restrictions.
* 2011 -- SB 234: Protected concealed carry permit holders from criminal penalties if their legally carried firearm was briefly or accidentally exposed and affirmed the right to carry a gun in your car.
* 2015 -- SB 290: Allowed lawful firearm owners to carry during mandatory evacuations in declared emergencies without a carry permit.
* 2016 -- HB 163: Broad pro-gun legislation that addressed open carry, firearms rights, concealed weapons arrests, and protections for concealed-carry licensees.
* 2016 -- HB 4001: Would have allowed concealed-carry licensees to openly carry handguns and carry firearms on college and university campuses.
* 2017 -- HB 245/SB 128: Strengthened Florida's self-defense and Stand Your Ground protections.
* 2017 -- HB 779: Would have reduced penalties for concealed-carry licensees who inadvertently or temporarily displayed a firearm.

I also voted for the Republican-led, bipartisan legislation supported by Governor Scott following the 2018 Parkland massacre. It raised the minimum age to purchase any firearm from 18 to 21 (the age for purchasing a handgun in Florida had already been 21 for decades) and allowed law enforcement to temporarily remove firearms from individuals posing a significant risk to themselves or others.
These measures were intended to address warning signs that were tragically present in the Parkland case: a 19-year-old with a documented history of mental-health problems and threats to shoot up his school. The law remains in effect today, with Republican majorities continuing to support it.
IMMIGRATION: The claim that I support illegal immigration is equally false. A secure border is fundamental to our national security, independence, and prosperity, and my record reflects my support for enforcing our immigration laws.

* 2017 -- CS/HB 697: This bill prohibited sanctuary policies and required state and local governments and law enforcement to cooperate with federal immigration authorities, including honoring detainers and sharing information. I voted for this in the Florida House, but it failed in the Senate.

* 2011 -- CS/HB 7089, This would have strengthened enforcement of federal immigration laws and employment verification. I voted in favor of this bill in Committee but it never received a final House vote.

I did vote to support tuition for Dreamers. These were young people who were brought here as children, and at the time, had federal authorization to remain in the United States and work. My vote was not a vote for open borders, sanctuary policies, amnesty, citizenship, or legal immigration status.
The Florida tuition legislation did none of those things. Immigration policy is, and should remain, a federal responsibility.
It was not an immigration bill and did not grant citizenship or legal status. Many of these students had grown up in Florida, attended our schools, played on our athletic teams, volunteered in our communities and churches, and knew no other home. I believed we could uphold the rule of law while recognizing the reality of their circumstances and their efforts to build a future through education. Reasonable people reached different conclusions, and I respect those who voted differently.
I am a conservative running to represent District 25 in Congress and continue the fight for our freedoms--a fight that began with my service as a United States Navy submarine warfare officer and continued through my eight years in the Florida House and as Chairman of the Broward Republican Party.
I will always talk straight and defend my position. I will never tell you one thing and do another. That you can count on!
Thank you again for your support, your prayers, and your willingness to help. Please make sure your friends and neighbors know when and where to vote.
God bless you and your families.
George

body:
# [](https://act.wesmoore.com/go/8?t=1&akid=1715%2E1086043%2EEnzInb)
Peter, it’s Dawn Moore.
Today's my birthday — and I have one wish. 🎂✨
Every year on this day, _I find myself thinking about why we do this._
I watch my husband show up for Maryland the same way he shows up for our family. Not because it's easy. **But because he genuinely believes every single person in this state deserves a real shot.**
The kids who need better schools. The family stretched thin by bills. The worker who just needs someone in his corner.
I see it at home. I see it on the road. I see it in the way he never stops.
We aren't doing this for politics. **We're doing this for people.**

Peter,
Last week, I had the chance to join _CNN_ and _MS Now_ to talk about our campaign and why this race is so important for Texans.

Texans in every corner of our state are ready for change because they are tired of paying more and getting less under Greg Abbott’s twelve years in office.

The outcome of our race will directly decide the balance of power in Congress and the White House.

**The future of our country truly depends on the outcome of this race.**
Right now, we’re within striking distance of making history. If we ride this momentum wave and reach every voter who is ready for a new direction, we can win this election and change the course of our state and nation.

Gina

clean_body: Peter, After the sudden death of my brother, Lindsey Graham, I was appointed by Governor Henry McMaster to represent South Carolina in the United States Senate. President Trump encouraged me to consider running in the Special Election by saying, "Run, Darline, Run!" Now, with the President's I've spent a lot of time talking and praying with my family. This was not a decision I made lightly. I know it will be difficult, I know what Lindsey cared about, and we shared the same conservative values. He cared deeply about the people of South Carolina. With what I learned from Lindsey and my nearly 30 years of helping people of the state find dignity through work, I am ready to take on this next challenge. It's time for me to step up for South Carolina, just like Lindsey stepped up for me when our parents died. I've learned God often calls on ordinary people to do extraordinary things in the most challenging of times. I am not Lindsey. I have my own way of doing things. But we were raised with the same values: work hard each day, trust in the Lord, remember your roots, and never forget who you work for. I did not seek this moment, Peter. But after many prayers and speaking with my family, I know I am making the right decision to run for this seat. I'll be straight with you - I am behind financially. My opponents are self-funding millionaires or have spent years building up their campaign war chests, but I'm new to politics. We've had only a few weeks to run against people who have been at this for years. Since you were there for Lindsey, Thank you for everything you did for Lindsey over the years. I know that having people like you in his corner meant everything to him. God bless, Darline Graham P.S. It's been a difficult couple of weeks. I never thought I'd be in this position, but I am ready to answer the call from President Trump. I am ready to run. | Paid for by the NRSC. clean_body: Josh Shapiro's far-right opponent went to DC for a photo op at the White House. | | | | BREAKING: Donald Trump just endorsed Stacy Garrity for a THIRD TIME in this race — and this time, while standing hand-in-hand in the Oval Office. This week, Josh Shapiro's far-right opponent left Pennsylvania for a photo op in the gilded Oval Office. And Derek, Donald Trump couldn’t have heaped more praise on her. Maybe it’s because she wants to bring Trump’s agenda of chaos, cruelty, and corruption to Pennsylvania “as soon as possible.” Maybe it’s because she called Trump’s disastrous healthcare cuts “the right thing to do.” Maybe it’s because she can’t name a single issue where she disagrees with Trump. body:
Tuesday was a record night.
# [](https://act.leaderswedeserve.com/go/852?refcode=em20260808-1&t=1&akid=3843%2E587540%2EAgqzOg)
Peter,
Earlier this week, this movement had a night we'll be talking about for a long time.
**Leaders We Deserve went 4 for 4 on Tuesday night!**
Donavan McKinney. Abbas Alawieh. Cat Clayton. Claire Heinrich.
Four incredible candidates. Four victories for the next generation of progressive leadership.
And none of it would have been possible without supporters like you.
The biggest victory of the night came in Michigan, where **Donavan McKinney became the first Leaders We Deserve-endorsed candidate this cycle to unseat a Democratic incumbent.**
Donavan built a campaign rooted in working-class communities, fixing our broken criminal justice system, investing in youth through education, and rebuilding our democracy. His victory sends a message that reaches far beyond one district: young, people-powered candidates can win — even against entrenched incumbents.
Also in Michigan, **Abbas Alawieh** earned a hard-fought victory after running on a vision centered around affordable housing, universal health care, and an economy that works for working people — not wealthy corporations.
In Missouri, **Cat Clayton** officially secured her place on the ballot after building a campaign focused on pushing for government transparency, everyday affordability, and labor and union rights.
Also in Missouri, **Claire Heinrich** officially advanced, bringing her bold vision for repairing infrastructure, investing in public education, and economic affordability one step closer to the state legislature.
These victories may have happened in different states, but they all have one thing in common: They were powered by people who believe our politics should belong to communities — not mega donors, corporate PACs, or the political elite.
**This is exactly why Leaders We Deserve exists.**
We're finding young leaders committed to genuine change, investing in them early, and proving that people-powered campaigns can win.
Tuesday wasn't the finish line.
It was proof that this movement is growing — and that together, we're building the next generation of progressive leadership across the country.

David Hogg

name: Gabby Giffords
subject: Lauren Boebert just introduced legislation to overturn the USPS’s ban on delivering handguns through the mail — a rule that has been in place for nearly 100 years. We need you to help us fight back.
disclaimer_text: Paid For By Giffords PAC; not authorized by any candidate or candidate's committee
body:
Please don’t skip this.
#

Friends: it’s Gabby Giffords. I wanted to make sure you saw this message from our team before the weekend ends.
If Lauren Boebert and the NRA get their way, the U.S. Postal Service could be on the verge of ending their century-old ban on mailing handguns. We need to speak out.
Please read the update below, then consider making a donation to help GIFFORDS PAC fight back. Thank you.
**[DONATE](https://go.giffords.org/go/14457?c0=giff-em-q32026.gsDos-&refcode=em260808-1-b&t=1&akid=11707%2E3935704%2Et7_-0E)**
* * *

❗ Friends — to everybody who cares about our fight for gun safety, please don’t skip this important message.
Lauren Boebert just introduced legislation that would overturn the USPS’s ban on mailing handguns that’s been in place since 1927. We need you to help fight back.

For nearly 100 years, federal law has prohibited the United States Postal Service from carrying or delivering handguns as mail — with exceptions for members of the military, law enforcement, or licensed gun manufacturers or dealers.
Lauren Boebert and Donald Trump are trying to change that.
[](https://go.giffords.org/go/14457?c0=giff-em-q32026.gsDos-&refcode=em260808-1-b&t=2&akid=11707%2E3935704%2Et7_-0E)
Donald Trump’s DOJ recently issued a memorandum saying they would no longer enforce this ban. Now, Boebert is trying to pass a bill that would officially let the USPS deliver guns through the mail — with no background checks, licensing, or training.

If this goes into effect, it would mean people who shouldn’t have a gun will be able to go around state and federal laws and get a gun mailed to them.
**This change also means that gun traffickers have a new way to move firearms through America’s communities.**
At a time when gun violence is the #1 killer of kids and teenagers in our country, this rule would make us all less safe. We need to fight back.

You have helped us so much to fight back against extremist legislation and pass gun safety laws. Now, we need your support again to fight back against Lauren Boebert and the gun lobby’s plans.
[**Please, will you donate $3 to help GIFFORDS PAC today? Our average online donation is around $27. Some give more, others give less. What matters most is that you are taking action today in the fight to make our communities safer.**](https://go.giffords.org/go/14457?c0=giff-em-q32026.gsDos-&refcode=em260808-1-b&t=3&akid=11707%2E3935704%2Et7_-0E)
