_**by Dan Perry and Cliff Schecter**_
Most historical turning points are obvious. Pearl Harbor. The assassination of John F. Kennedy. September 11. At the time, people understand they are witnessing events that will shape everything that follows--often in ways that cannot yet understand.
December 12, 2000, was different.
Quick, what happened that day? You don't know? That puts you in the company of most Americans.
And yet there is a serious argument that no day during the past quarter century--and few in U.S. history--had greater long-term consequences on the health, wealth and welfare of our republic. That was the day the Supreme Court--in a partisan 5-4 decision that will live in infamy--decided in _Bush v. Gore_ to ignore the traditional role of states in administering their elections (as laid out in the Constitution) and shut down vote counting in Florida with an unnecessary, arbitrary deadline, and "selected" George W. Bush as the 43rd President of the United States."
The highly partisan decision reeked of bias and corruption.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/c1674416-14a1-42ba-aa09-cae0321aeb84?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
The Florida Governor at the time was none other than George W. Bush's brother Jeb. Four of the five members of the right-wing majority that ruled in favor of Bush had been elevated to The Court during the presidency or vice presidency of his father, George H.W. Bush. And what was done that day in Washington likely altered the trajectory of American foreign policy, constitutional law, political institutions, and even the political culture from which later presidents emerged, in ways both profound and incredibly harmful to the American republic.
In fact, it could be argued that that day was the beginning of the division, decadence, and decay of American democracy we've witnessed over the past quarter century. In short, it kicked off a long decline - with a few interregnums providing the illusion of hope - of the United States as a superpower that commanded the respect of the world.
This is, of course, a counterfactual, and counterfactuals can never be proved. Yet almost twenty-six years later, enough has happened that some consequences appear remarkably direct, while others remain likely or plausible, even if impossible to establish with certainty. Taken together, they suggest that one of the defining moments of modern American history was not a war, a terrorist attack, or an election night.
It was a Supreme Court decision issued on an otherwise ordinary Tuesday afternoon. The banality of evil, as they say. That it was a 5-4 decision split down partisan lines - after the Supreme Court had spent years trying to decide the most controversial cases unanimously, or with strong majorities so as to limit division among the American populace (Brown vs Board, for example, was unanimous, while Roe v. Wade was decided 7-1, with one justice abstaining) couldn't have been more apropos.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/c1674416-14a1-42ba-aa09-cae0321aeb84?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* * *
### **The war that probably never happens**
The strongest argument concerns Iraq.
Whether Al Gore could have actually prevented the attacks on September 11 is impossible to know--though as a policy wonk one could guess he wouldn't have been clearing brush on a Texas ranch discussing ending stem-cell research while presidential briefings were being created by his national security team with titles like "Bin Laden Determined ot Strike in the U.S." A reasonable assessment is a Gore Administration would have been less likely to miss vital and available intelligence,, and would have devoted greater attention to terrorism.
Had the attacks occurred under President Gore, the United States would almost certainly still have attacked Afghanistan. The Taliban was sheltering al-Qaeda, NATO invoked Article 5 for the first time in its history, and there was overwhelming international support for military action against those responsible.
But Iraq, well, that is another matter entirely.
That invasion reflected the worldview of George W. Bush and many of the advisers surrounding him. Several of them had advocated removing Saddam Hussein long before September 11. It also required a culture of lying which, frankly, sits more naturally with a Republican administration. Even putting aside fake intel about weapons of mass destruction, Saddam simply had no connection to 9-11, yet an implied connection was key in their selling of this war.
Gore - much more of a stickler for facts - publicly opposed the invasion before it occurred, arguing that it diverted attention from al-Qaeda and risked creating precisely the instability it claimed it would eliminate. It is impossible to exclude every imaginable scenario in which a Gore administration eventually confronted Iraq, but it is extraordinarily difficult to construct a realistic path leading to the 2003 invasion as it actually happened.
That single difference alters an astonishing amount of subsequent history.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/c1674416-14a1-42ba-aa09-cae0321aeb84?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
The Iraq War consumed trillions of dollars, claimed hundreds of thousands of lives, strained alliances, and inflicted lasting damage on American credibility. The "de-Baathification" process, which removed anyone who served the regime, was plainly a mistake that left chaos in its wake; that requires a GOP-level indifference to expert counsel - sort of like the party's position with climate denial, vaccine science, trickle-down economics and many other issues.
By destroying Saddam Hussein's regime, it also removed Iran's principal regional rival and unintentionally expanded Tehran's influence across the Middle East. The collapse of the Iraqi state, the insurgency that followed, and the conditions from which ISIS eventually emerged all trace part of their origins to that decision. The insane level of regional tensions confronting the United States today - with a maximally hubristic Iran at the center - are difficult to understand without Iraq.
The consequences extended far beyond foreign policy. Iraq profoundly damaged public confidence in our government. Intelligence agencies, military intervention, foreign-policy expertise, and the judgment of political leaders all became objects of deep public skepticism. The belief that America's governing class had made a catastrophic mistake became one of the defining political facts of the early twenty-first century.
Some of the horrific and illegal outgrowths of 9/11 - torture and its justifications, preventative war, rendition, the loss of privacy, the erosion of due process, the creation of a giant gulag in Guantanamo Bay, the placement of unqualified cronies in key government positions (heckuva job, Brownie!) - can be viewed as the seeds of today's fully grown lawlessness we've seen under Donald Trump's Defense Department, Justice Department, ICE, and more.
Alongside war and terrorism, climate change presents a different kind of counterfactual. Long before it became a central political issue, Gore had made global warming one of his defining causes. It is difficult to imagine a Gore administration withdrawing from the Kyoto Protocol, elevating fossil-fuel production as a central priority, or treating climate science with the skepticism that characterized much of the Bush years. At the very least, the United States would almost certainly have entered the twenty-first century with a markedly different posture toward what many now regard as its greatest long-term challenge.
If the worst predictions about climate change prove correct -- rising seas swallowing coastal cities, vast regions becoming too hot for human habitation, hundreds of millions displaced by drought and famine, ecosystems collapsing, and geopolitical conflict intensifying over food and water - those humans left to clean up the mess will have the 2000 Court to thank.

Yet almost twenty-six years later, enough has happened that some consequences appear remarkably direct, while others remain likely or plausible, even if impossible to establish with certainty. Taken together, they suggest that one of the defining moments of modern American history was not a war, a terrorist attack, or an election night. It was a Supreme Court decision issued on an otherwise ordinary Tuesday afternoon. The banality of evil, as they say. That it was a 5-4 decision split down partisan lines - after the Supreme Court had spent years trying to decide the most controversial cases unanimously, or with strong majorities so as to limit division among the American populace (Brown vs Board, for example, was unanimous, while Roe v. Wade was decided 7-1, with one justice abstaining) couldn't have been more apropos. | | ---|---|--- The war that probably never happens** The strongest argument concerns Iraq. Whether Al Gore could have actually prevented the attacks on September 11 is impossible to know--though as a policy wonk one could guess he wouldn't have been clearing brush on a Texas ranch discussing ending stem-cell research while presidential briefings were being created by his national security team with titles like "Bin Laden Determined ot Strike in the U.S." A reasonable assessment is a Gore Administration would have been less likely to miss vital and available intelligence,, and would have devoted greater attention to terrorism. Had the attacks occurred under President Gore, the United States would almost certainly still have attacked Afghanistan. The Taliban was sheltering al-Qaeda, NATO invoked Article 5 for the first time in its history, and there was overwhelming international support for military action against those responsible. But Iraq, well, that is another matter entirely. That invasion reflected the worldview of George W. Bush and many of the advisers surrounding him. Several of them had advocated removing Saddam Hussein long before September 11. It also required a culture of lying which, frankly, sits more naturally with a Republican administration. Even putting aside fake intel about weapons of mass destruction, Saddam simply had no connection to 9-11, yet an implied connection was key in their selling of this war. Gore - much more of a stickler for facts - publicly opposed the invasion before it occurred, arguing that it diverted attention from al-Qaeda and risked creating precisely the instability it claimed it would eliminate. It is impossible to exclude every imaginable scenario in which a Gore administration eventually confronted Iraq, but it is extraordinarily difficult to construct a realistic path leading to the 2003 invasion as it actually happened. That single difference alters an astonishing amount of subsequent history. | | ---|---|--- The Iraq War consumed trillions of dollars, claimed hundreds of thousands of lives, strained alliances, and inflicted lasting damage on American credibility. The "de-Baathification" process, which removed anyone who served the regime, was plainly a mistake that left chaos in its wake; that requires a GOP-level indifference to expert counsel - sort of like the party's position with climate denial, vaccine science, trickle-down economics and many other issues. By destroying Saddam Hussein's regime, it also removed Iran's principal regional rival and unintentionally expanded Tehran's influence across the Middle East. The collapse of the Iraqi state, the insurgency that followed, and the conditions from which ISIS eventually emerged all trace part of their origins to that decision. The insane level of regional tensions confronting the United States today - with a maximally hubristic Iran at the center - are difficult to understand without Iraq. The consequences extended far beyond foreign policy. Iraq profoundly damaged public confidence in our government. Intelligence agencies, military intervention, foreign-policy expertise, and the judgment of political leaders all became objects of deep public skepticism. The belief that America's governing class had made a catastrophic mistake became one of the defining political facts of the early twenty-first century. Some of the horrific and illegal outgrowths of 9/11 - torture and its justifications, preventative war, rendition, the loss of privacy, the erosion of due process, the creation of a giant gulag in Guantanamo Bay, the placement of unqualified cronies in key government positions (heckuva job, Brownie!) - can be viewed as the seeds of today's fully grown lawlessness we've seen under Donald Trump's Defense Department, Justice Department, ICE, and more. Alongside war and terrorism, climate change presents a different kind of counterfactual. Long before it became a central political issue, Gore had made global warming one of his defining causes. It is difficult to imagine a Gore administration withdrawing from the Kyoto Protocol, elevating fossil-fuel production as a central priority, or treating climate science with the skepticism that characterized much of the Bush years. At the very least, the United States would almost certainly have entered the twenty-first century with a markedly different posture toward what many now regard as its greatest long-term challenge. If the worst predictions about climate change prove correct -- rising seas swallowing coastal cities, vast regions becoming too hot for human habitation, hundreds of millions displaced by drought and famine, ecosystems collapsing, and geopolitical conflict intensifying over food and water - those humans left to clean up the mess will have the 2000 Court to thank. | | SUBSCRIBER-ONLY POLL Your view of the Supreme Court Selection of Bush in 2000? | ? ? ? ? ? All of that was the foreign policy. The domestic consequence is worse, and it's still sitting on the bench. Everything above is the part most people have at least half-heard. What follows is the part almost nobody connects back to a Tuesday in December. Fellow American Patriot,Mike Lindell here, founder of MyPillow and [_**candidate for Minnesota Governor.**_](http://links.conservativesdefendingfreedom.com/u/click?_t=91d01aa68bbe4105984439520ca0f0af&_m=d3b946d991864aa587c0d14310763a6b&_e=KJoVENahzcSm-AahSgRGr4OhAVSAc0T5wviHkGBKFIF7qfnMGznM6C-EK37_V9l80QrkyuRzd4BFrojMD_lOkC1fzsl3WDTs6t6OMCWS3lNStqNdd9WX-EC0aNthZCS2jNU1TOWZLlr2JeqFC_xs_FHBZ4WYcrkPq0Nz4My_tZBxXJsaXCm04Ujl4FuaKRRo_RFpqTIrUxZmGOdWAtCQopMfT4VXpIkRIIpooMaVByy2ZQ1SjfgK8uc7ym_IJBSUtDNl-FUdmUIZ1CY0wlTsWPnVE0FYJQzGo4JAniigExwkt16c3-pUKQnVgAJq31HMRflv_XV8XAy8lgK3lmV9M6qmHYRtGLVHk2b3Rm1tO1rCaZyE0fPfrLae3tUDz82JKNiSTu7JaAb8j8h-sbPXDQ%3D%3D) I'm reaching out because this week, I made one of the biggest decisions of my life.After 22 years leading the company I founded, I've stepped down as CEO of MyPillow.I didn't make that decision lightly.For more than two decades, MyPillow has been my life's work. Together, we built a Minnesota company from the ground up, created jobs, and proved that with faith, perseverance, and hard work, incredible things are still possible in this wonderful country.So why would I step away now?[**It's simple: because Minnesota deserves a Governor who is 100% committed.**](http://links.conservativesdefendingfreedom.com/u/click?_t=91d01aa68bbe4105984439520ca0f0af&_m=d3b946d991864aa587c0d14310763a6b&_e=KJoVENahzcSm-AahSgRGr4OhAVSAc0T5wviHkGBKFIF7qfnMGznM6C-EK37_V9l80QrkyuRzd4BFrojMD_lOkC1fzsl3WDTs6t6OMCWS3lNStqNdd9WX-EC0aNthZCS2jNU1TOWZLlr2JeqFC_xs_FHBZ4WYcrkPq0Nz4My_tZBxXJsaXCm04Ujl4FuaKRRo_RFpqTIrUxZmGOdWAtCQopMfT4VXpIkRIIpooMaVByy2ZQ1SjfgK8uc7ym_IJBSUESdAbGs5JcHUG9zfDSulMGIKf0_kvFF-AOEXCG5CGBJljcl9VRcDXiulfijliLNznEVeZz69fKTRbrTGhFNAf_8EA2Fm8S_XlIX7Knfxn79IR72eU5XgwYJt7YvNRkOPcjvkT0-dWe-NdGoVwyJTuA%3D%3D) Minnesota deserves my complete focus, my full energy, and my undivided attention.I'm all in. 100% -- And today I'm hoping you're all in too.[**Will you click here to make a generous contribution to my campaign to take back our state and make Minnesota Great Again?**](http://links.conservativesdefendingfreedom.com/u/click?_t=91d01aa68bbe4105984439520ca0f0af&_m=d3b946d991864aa587c0d14310763a6b&_e=KJoVENahzcSm-AahSgRGr4OhAVSAc0T5wviHkGBKFIF7qfnMGznM6C-EK37_V9l80QrkyuRzd4BFrojMD_lOkC1fzsl3WDTs6t6OMCWS3lNStqNdd9WX-EC0aNthZCS2jNU1TOWZLlr2JeqFC_xs_FHBZ4WYcrkPq0Nz4My_tZBxXJsaXCm04Ujl4FuaKRRo_RFpqTIrUxZmGOdWAtCQopMfT4VXpIkRIIpooMaVByy2ZQ1SjfgK8uc7ym_IJBSUkAX4GlAetqdQLq_Tkx4wIWoZR_sNMZzhj3PYSIWhDt5iPOPymt_S5vvFByJ91lDBPCVinb6Rv2zvbDWh6Vp4s3mVFRrJmNXwM1pdghQ1rKnRMaa0Bf4WLL2d8k4UJ_ejc56TOrONvapoAK6c4O0Ylw%3D%3D) My friend, this decision wasn't about walking away. It's about stepping up for you. Career politicians spend their lives protecting what's best for themselves. They worry about their next title, their next election, and their next opportunity. I'm choosing a different path. I'm putting Minnesota ahead of myself. I'm choosing the fight to save Minnesota and I'm giving it my all. I don't have a backup plan.I'm all in. President Trump honored me with his endorsement because he knows I'll fight for Minnesota without compromise.Now I'm backing up those words and his confidence with action by giving 100% to this campaign.But I can't do it by myself. **[I need grassroots conservatives across Minnesota-and across the country-standing with me.](http://links.conservativesdefendingfreedom.com/u/click?_t=91d01aa68bbe4105984439520ca0f0af&_m=d3b946d991864aa587c0d14310763a6b&_e=KJoVENahzcSm-AahSgRGr4OhAVSAc0T5wviHkGBKFIF7qfnMGznM6C-EK37_V9l80QrkyuRzd4BFrojMD_lOkC1fzsl3WDTs6t6OMCWS3lNStqNdd9WX-EC0aNthZCS2jNU1TOWZLlr2JeqFC_xs_FHBZ4WYcrkPq0Nz4My_tZBxXJsaXCm04Ujl4FuaKRRo_RFpqTIrUxZmGOdWAtCQopMfT4VXpIkRIIpooMaVByy2ZQ1SjfgK8uc7ym_IJBSU659dDLm3Aw0wdP3iehGoqcNZL7QfHDyibg3F5YtFjFyWeOPN95H50gULNecQ7OrE56HWFrFsZFA69UKgoRZPTxPe2-uhcKLAUvGDMIu2lrzwBlZLk5s4NE_aClPF83eGCvG4x19T06gk3jXEeUqqng%3D%3D)**_**_Every phone call we make..._**__**_Every yard sign we print..._**__**_Every door we knock..._**__**_Every voter we reach..._**_ It's only possible because people like you decide this campaign is worth fighting for.**If you believe Minnesota deserves a Governor who's willing to sacrifice, willing to lead, and willing to put our state first, I'm asking you to stand with me today.****[Will you make a contribution of $10, $25, $50, or whatever you can afford to help me win this race?](http://links.conservativesdefendingfreedom.com/u/click?_t=91d01aa68bbe4105984439520ca0f0af&_m=d3b946d991864aa587c0d14310763a6b&_e=KJoVENahzcSm-AahSgRGr4OhAVSAc0T5wviHkGBKFIF7qfnMGznM6C-EK37_V9l80QrkyuRzd4BFrojMD_lOkC1fzsl3WDTs6t6OMCWS3lNStqNdd9WX-EC0aNthZCS2jNU1TOWZLlr2JeqFC_xs_FHBZ4WYcrkPq0Nz4My_tZBxXJsaXCm04Ujl4FuaKRRo_RFpqTIrUxZmGOdWAtCQopMfT4VXpIkRIIpooMaVByy2ZQ1SjfgK8uc7ym_IJBSUJkhT1EMPTmGM_9KhzFaopBvGI23rPhsvwFEqYGJbntx8pLVzFCSpiKNvMHoHXvldffnCD1xhTQi2QNEL0tcHUbF89iQG9SvRgji1BdAMIgzjECCWXP1U2hvtpUQdtV6aFC4AKOvfFuXqy4abpYHNsQ%3D%3D)****_Together, we can save Minnesota._** **_I'm all in. That took some serious _chutzpah_. My great-grandfather believed so strongly in the promise of America – a place where he could be Jewish without fear, where he could forge his own path – that he left his whole world behind. That promise came true for him, and for generations of my family. That’s what sets America apart. Here, anyone with a little _chutzpah_ is free to be whoever they want to be, do whatever they want to do, and achieve more than they ever dreamed. In 1993, I joined the Navy to defend those freedoms. In 2018, I ran for Congress to expand them. In 2020, I won re-election to continue that work, making our nation free, safe, and prosperous. In 2022, I served on the January 6th Committee because our Constitutional freedoms were threatened. In 2026, I’m the Democratic nominee for VA-02, because Jen Kiggans either _can’t or won’t_ protect them. The fact is that Hampton Roads is in crisis. Our community’s been hit hard by this president’s failed agenda. **It's time for a leader with _chutzpah_.** **I just won my primary, and now the real fight begins.** VA-02 is rated a Toss-Up, dark money groups and super PACs are circling. This will be one of the toughest, costliest fights of the entire 2026 election cycle. Luckily, _chutzpah_ runs in my family, and I’m not afraid of a little mishigas. clean_body: I don’t fly a helicopter | = Peter, when public service asks for sacrifice, some people answer with action, and others find ways to profit. = As mayor, I turned down the city car. I did it because public service is about working for the people, not about personal benefit. My family shares two cars across three adults and two kids. A shared family car is how many people in NEPA get around town. That’s why it stings to see Rob Bresnahan fly around in his secret $1M helicopter (yes, a helicopter), play the stock market, and slash the healthcare families rely on. Rob Bresnahan is out of touch with NEPA. He voted to rip coverage away from tens of thousands of people in our region, personally profited off that vote via his stock trading, and then showed up at our hospitals for photo ops as if nothing happened. That is not leadership. That is looking out for yourself. If we want a Congress that understands how our towns and counties actually work, we need more mayors and county commissioners in Washington. We know how to fix a bridge, build a park, and get things done without letting insiders profit. Fellow Patriot - I'm not a politician. In fact, I've never run for office before.

I never expected to be running for office. I have never had any desire to be a politician. I am doing this because I am answering President Donald Trump's call to serve and want to stand up for South Carolina and fight for his agenda.

_**Like Lindsey, I am a hard worker with a servant's heart.**_ We grew up in the back of a bar and liquor store, in one room. Our parents worked hard every day to make ends meet - there was no time for sickness and few vacations, because if the doors weren't open, no money was coming in.

What I've spent my life doing is serving South Carolina - including running a state agency with 130 employees and a $90 million budget. We turned it from a struggling organization into a national model helping people find work and live independently. We made sure all spending was reasonable, allowable, and necessary. _I fought against duplication of services, knowing it wasted taxpayers' dollars_.

clean_body: I am answering President Donald Trump's call to serve and want to stand up for South Carolina and fight for his agenda. | Fellow Patriot - I'm not a politician. In fact, I've never run for office before. I never expected to be running for office. I have never had any desire to be a politician. I am doing this because I am answering President Donald Trump's call to serve and want to stand up for South Carolina and fight for his agenda. Like Lindsey, I am a hard worker with a servant's heart. We grew up in the back of a bar and liquor store, in one room. Our parents worked hard every day to make ends meet - there was no time for sickness and few vacations, because if the doors weren't open, no money was coming in. What I've spent my life doing is serving South Carolina - including running a state agency with 130 employees and a $90 million budget. We turned it from a struggling organization into a national model helping people find work and live independently. We made sure all spending was reasonable, allowable, and necessary. I fought against duplication of services, knowing it wasted taxpayers' dollars. I'm a mother, a grandmother, and a wife, and now South Carolina's first female United States Senator, I know how to bargain shop, and I look for the buy-one-get-one-free sales at the grocery store. I just bought a new pair of shoes to walk around the U.S. Capitol off the clearance rack at the Shoe Warehouse. I cut my own grass with a push mower, and yes, I know how to use a weed eater. I support the Right to Life. I believe in showing ID to vote to save our country. I oppose DEI. I think AOC is C-R-A-Z-Y. I think Anthony Fauci should stop staring at the floor and answer the questions. I stand for the national anthem. I believe our veterans are heroes. I will always Back the Blue. And I know that President Trump and I will Make America Great Again. I am the first woman United States senator in South Carolina history. My Democratic opponent, Dr. Annie Andrews, must not be the second. She supports turning confused little boys into little girls and vice versa. I believe that makes her the worst pediatrician in the country. President Trump wants a fighter in the Senate. That's exactly why he's in my corner in this race. Thanks, Darline Graham P.S. I'm not a politician. I'm a hard worker who answered President Trump's call to serve. Friends,

_**You heard right.**_ Donald Trump just gave Jerri Green the _strongest possible_ endorsement. When _Donald Trump_ hands out _his "Complete and Total Endorsement"_ to Marsha Blackburn,_they may think they’ve got Tennesseans fooled._ **But they are _completely_ misreading the room.**

Across our state, we’re seeing more and more lifelong Republicans waking up to what corrupt grifters like _Trump and Blackburn_ are really doing to our country and to Tennessee.

**Tennesseans are _sick and tired_ of the cruelty, _the corporate handouts_ , the draining of public schools into _private voucher schemes_ , and the _constant division_.** Tennesseans are _struggling_ to pay rent and put food on the table, and Marsha is talking about spies from China.Tennesseans need _affordable, accessible healthcare,_ not _never-ending warfare._ People want their kids to be able to _afford a future_ in the state where they were raised, while groceries, the cost of housing, utilities , and everything else continue to soar. Tennesseans have seen it first hand; their once thriving communities that have been _gutted by 20 years of failed Republican leadership,_ and _**they know something has to change.**_ **So when Trump stamps his approval on Blackburn _(like he did with Andy Ogles right before he lost race)_ , it sends a message,__just not the one he thinks.__** **For Tennesseans that are hurting and _tired of feeling left behind:_**
* **_Jerri has made over 150 stops across the state of Tennessee_ connecting directly with everyday people**, whereas Marsha _hides behind controlled photo-ops_ , has a habit of _dodging questions_ , and _repeating rehearsed talking points_ when faced with unscripted inquiries from constituents _(if they can find her)._
* **Jerri is committed to _fully funding public classrooms_ ,** raising teacher respect, and eliminating private school voucher schemes that drain local resources; Marsha's record backs policies that siphon taxpayer dollars away from our children's futures.
* **Jerri champions _expanding Medicaid_** to protect rural hospitals and working families, fighting for paid family leave, and lowering the cost of housing and childcare, while Marsha continues to push policies favoring corporate interests, including her support for Big Pharma and her active role in fueling Tennessee's opioid crisis by stripping the DEA of its power to crack down on suspicious pill shipments, over working Tennesseans.

**Jerri Green certainly _doesn’t_ have Donald Trump's blessing, and _that’s a good thing._ She does have something else _that no amount of billionaire backing can buy,_ the real excitement and energy of _everyday Tennesseans, coming together to do something new in Tennessee._** **We also can't ignore this _glaring weakness_ in Blackburn's campaign strategy: **Following historic primary turnout, Marsha put up a _remarkably weak_ primary performance. Peter,

After the sudden death of my brother, Lindsey Graham, I was appointed by Governor Henry McMaster to represent South Carolina in the United States Senate.

**President Trump encouraged me to consider running in the Special Election by saying, "Run, Darline, Run!" Now, with the President's _"Complete and Total Endorsement," I'm running to represent South Carolina for a full term in the United States Senate._**

I've spent a lot of time talking and praying with my family. This was not a decision I made lightly. I know it will be difficult, _**but I am ready.**_

I know what Lindsey cared about, and we shared the same conservative values. He cared deeply about the people of South Carolina. With what I learned from Lindsey and my nearly 30 years of helping people of the state find dignity through work, I am ready to take on this next challenge.

It's time for me to step up for South Carolina, just like Lindsey stepped up for me when our parents died. I've learned God often calls on ordinary people to do extraordinary things in the most challenging of times.

clean_body: | Peter, After the sudden death of my brother, Lindsey Graham, I was appointed by Governor Henry McMaster to represent South Carolina in the United States Senate. President Trump encouraged me to consider running in the Special Election by saying, "Run, Darline, Run!" Now, with the President's "Complete and Total Endorsement," I'm running to represent South Carolina for a full term in the United States Senate. I've spent a lot of time talking and praying with my family. This was not a decision I made lightly. I know it will be difficult, but I am ready. I know what Lindsey cared about, and we shared the same conservative values. He cared deeply about the people of South Carolina. With what I learned from Lindsey and my nearly 30 years of helping people of the state find dignity through work, I am ready to take on this next challenge. It's time for me to step up for South Carolina, just like Lindsey stepped up for me when our parents died. I've learned God often calls on ordinary people to do extraordinary things in the most challenging of times. I am not Lindsey. I have my own way of doing things. But we were raised with the same values: work hard each day, trust in the Lord, remember your roots, and never forget who you work for. I did not seek this moment, Peter. But after many prayers and speaking with my family, I know I am making the right decision to run for this seat. I'll be straight with you - I am behind financially. My opponents are self-funding millionaires or have spent years building up their campaign war chests, but I'm new to politics. We have less than 3 weeks to run against people who have been at this for years. Since you were there for Lindsey, Thank you for everything you did for Lindsey over the years. I know that having people like you in his corner meant everything to him. God bless, Darline Graham P.S. It's been a difficult week. I never thought I'd be in this position, but I am ready to answer the call from President Trump. I am ready to run. | | Paid for by Darline for Senate Don't want to receive any more of our emails? Peter, [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/136873034/638879171/1927019199?refcode=ITT_ATA_EM_FR_Dembo_2600808_T1_1&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNjEvMS8xMTAzNjMiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiYWMxNjJkOWUtNDI5My1mMTExLTliMzMtMDAwZDNhMTFmYTMwIiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=OPt5Cv2wvngu588LE9N8LxfWfpXlxH9Zqmr5qs9rmJ4=) I just released a new episode of my podcast featuring Zach Dembo, and I wanted you to know his story before you listen.

Zach is a federal prosecutor, a Navy JAG veteran, and a former policy advisor in my administration. He's spent his entire career serving this country with honor and without looking for credit.

Then he watched the Department of Justice be turned into a weapon for the powerful instead of a shield for the people. And instead of staying quiet to protect his career, Zach resigned from a job he loved. That's the kind of character we need representing Central Kentucky in Congress.

Now Zach's running to flip Kentucky's 6th Congressional District, and this race is closer than anyone expected. Two polls already show him tied with his opponent — Matt Bevin’s former running mate — and Cook Political Report just moved this race in his direction. This is exactly the kind of seat Democrats need to take back the House, in exactly the kind of district where a candidate like Zach can win, by being honest with people and focused on what actually matters to their lives.

His opponent, Ralph Alvarado, was Matt Bevin's running mate in 2019. We beat that ticket once, and we can do it again. Alvarado has a record of voting to protect nursing homes he personally worked for, some of them rated one star, while working families in this district struggle with rising costs and a Congress that won't lift a finger for them. Zach's already said he'll fight to ban congressional stock trading and end the culture of corruption that's made Washington work for the wealthy and connected instead of everyday people.

Coworkers. Neighbors. People who have been American citizens for decades are being told that status can be reopened.
The administration has directed immigration officials to refer 100 to 200 cases for denaturalization _every month._ 1 The Justice Department described it as the largest coordinated denaturalization effort in its history, and said it is "only the beginning."2

There is an old rule in politics:
**If you don 't vote, you can't complain about the results.**
I think about that every time I am out talking with voters. I knock on doors. I go to events. I talk with people at stores, restaurants, town meetings and Republican gatherings across the district.
_And I hear the complaints._
* Healthcare costs too much.
* The electric bill is outrageous.
* I-95 is a parking lot.
* Young people cannot afford to stay in Connecticut.
* Businesses are struggling.
* People are worried that artificial intelligence is going to eliminate jobs faster than we can create new ones.
* Parents are worried about the future their children will inherit.
* Seniors are worried about whether they can afford to stay in their homes.
* And nearly everyone believes Washington is not working the way it should.

**I hear you.**
In fact, many of those same frustrations are exactly why I am running for Congress.
But there comes a point when:
* complaining is not enough.
* posting on social media is not enough.
* when telling your friends what is wrong with the country is not enough.

_**Eventually, you have to vote.**_
## And that moment is now.
Early voting continues this weekend, Saturday, August 8 and Sunday, August 9.
The Republican primary is Tuesday, August 11.
It is August. People are away. Families are getting ready for school. There is no statewide race dominating television coverage or reminding everyone that an election is happening.
That means turnout matters even more.
In a low-turnout primary, **the people who show up make the decision for everyone else.**
I am asking you not to let someone else make that decision for you.
And I am asking you to vote for me.
## Why Goldstein?
For those who have followed this Substack, you know who I am.
**Doctor. Lawyer. Father. Fighter.**
I am also the **Republican Party-endorsed candidate for Congress in Connecticut 's Fourth Congressional District.**
Two years ago, I fought through a Republican primary and became our nominee for Congress in November 2024.
I could have gone home after the 2024 election, but I didn't.
* I kept showing up.
* I kept speaking out.
* I kept traveling to Washington.
* I kept advocating.
* I kept working on the issues that matter to Connecticut even though I did not have a congressional title in front of my name.

Why?
Because I believe public service should be about more than getting elected.
**You should not have to wait until you are in office to start fighting for the people you want to represent.**
_That is why I have reached out directly to federal officials multiple times, including Secretary of Energy Chris Wright and EPA Administrator Lee Zeldin, about problems affecting Connecticut._
I am doing it now.
**Imagine what I can do with a seat in Congress.**
## I Bring a Different Skill Set
I have said throughout this campaign that I bring a different skill set to this race.
I mean that.
I am not a career politician.
I am a physician who has spent decades dealing with one of the most complicated and expensive systems in America.
I know healthcare because I live healthcare.
I know what patients go through.
I know what doctors go through.
I know what happens when bureaucracy gets between a patient and care.
I have also led medical societies and organizations. I have run a small business. I have had to balance budgets and make payroll.
Later in life, I became a lawyer.
So when we talk about healthcare, business, regulation, law and government, I am not approaching these subjects from a talking-points sheet or some tweet.
**I have actually lived them.**
And Washington could use more people who have spent their lives solving problems outside of Washington.
## Healthcare Is Not Just Another Issue to Me
Healthcare represents roughly one-fifth of the American economy.
Yet
* Families continue to pay more.
* Employers continue to pay more.
* Government continues to spend more.
* And patients frequently feel as if they have fewer choices.

Something is wrong with that equation.
I believe we need greater competition, greater transparency and more meaningful choice.
Healthcare should be centered around the patient -- not around insurance companies, bureaucracies or government systems.
This is one of the clearest differences I bring to this race.
**I have spent my career taking care of patients.**
If healthcare affordability is one of the defining challenges facing American families, perhaps sending someone to Congress who actually understands healthcare would be a good place to start.
## Connecticut Cannot Be Affordable Without Affordable Energy
Then there is energy.
Talk to almost any homeowner or business owner in Connecticut and eventually the conversation gets to the electric bill.
High energy costs do not stop with your utility bill.
They increase the cost of running a store.
They increase the cost of manufacturing.
They increase the cost of refrigerating and transporting food.
They make Connecticut less competitive.
Ultimately, those costs get passed back to all of us.
That is why I have been pushing the energy issue and communicating with federal officials.
We need more energy supply and the infrastructure necessary to bring it into New England.
**You cannot seriously talk about affordability in Connecticut without talking about energy.**
## And Can We Finally Admit That I-95 Is a Parking Lot?
Then there is infrastructure.
There is nothing particularly "interstate" about Interstate 95 when you spend half your life sitting still on it and most use it to travel only 17 miles.
For decades we have heard about studies, plans and projects.
Meanwhile, commuters lose hours - Almost 4 weeks of work a year because they have to leave their houses earlier to be on time.
Businesses lose productivity.
Parents lose time with their families.
Our infrastructure problem is an economic problem and a quality-of-life problem.
We need representatives in Washington who understand that federal policy is not some distant theoretical exercise.
**Federal decisions have local consequences.**
That is one of the central ideas behind my campaign: finding **federal solutions to local problems.**
## We Also Have to Prepare for What Comes Next
Artificial intelligence is already transforming the workforce.
Pretending otherwise will not protect our children.
We need to make sure Connecticut students are prepared for an economy in which many traditional jobs will change and some will disappear altogether.
That means college for students for whom college makes sense.
But it also means something we have undervalued for far too long:
* **The trades.**
* Technical education.
* Apprenticeships.
* Skilled manufacturing.
* Construction.
* Healthcare careers.
* Infrastructure jobs.
* Careers requiring human judgment, physical skill and real-world expertise that cannot simply be replaced by an algorithm.

I want Connecticut to build an **AI-proof workforce.**
We should be creating pathways that allow young people to graduate into real jobs, build careers and remain here in Connecticut.
## This Election Really Comes Down to a Few Questions
When you vote, ask yourself:
* Who understands healthcare well enough to help fix it?
* Who understands what it means to run a business and balance a budget?
* Who is willing to fight for more affordable energy?
* Who will push to get infrastructure moving?
* Who is thinking about how Connecticut's young people will compete in an AI-driven economy?
* Who is already going to Washington and advocating before ever being elected?

And ultimately:
* **Who is best prepared to take on Jim Himes in November?**

I know the answer is Dr. Michael Goldstein and that is why I am asking for your vote.
## Stop Complaining. Start Voting.
There is a temptation in politics to think:
"My vote won't matter."
Especially in an August primary.
But think about what that actually means.
Elections are not decided by the people who planned to vote.
They are not decided by people who complain about politics at dinner.
They are not decided by Facebook posts.
They are not decided by yard signs.
They are not decided by the people who say, "Someone needs to do something."
**They are decided by the people who show up.**
So:
* If healthcare matters to you, **Vote Goldstein.**
* If affordability matters to you, **Vote Goldstein.**
* If energy matters to you, **Vote Goldstein.**
* If jobs matter to you, **Vote Goldstein.**
* If infrastructure matters to you, **Vote Goldstein.**
* If you want young people to have a future here in Connecticut, **Vote Goldstein.**

And if you believe it is time for a different kind of representative to take on Jim Himes:
**Vote Goldstein.**
You do not have to agree with me on every issue and I don't expect you to.
What I ask is that you look at my background, look at what I have been doing, look at my willingness to fight, and decide who you want standing in the ring in November.
But first, we have to get through August 11.
### EARLY VOTING
**Saturday, August 8**
**Sunday, August 9**
### REPUBLICAN PRIMARY DAY
# TUESDAY, AUGUST 11
I am the Republican Party-endorsed candidate for Congress.
I respectfully ask for your support and your vote.
**Doctor. Lawyer. Father. Fighter.**
# Vote Goldstein for Congress.
**Stop complaining. Start voting.**
Because if you stay home, someone else gets to make the decision for you.

On August 11, don't let someone else decide who takes the fight to Jim Himes in November. | | ---|---|--- | | | Forwarded this email? ? for more The Goldstein Substack - A Father-Son Publication Dr. Goldstein is Running for Congress and his page can be found Early voting continues this weekend. On August 11, don't let someone else decide who takes the fight to Jim Himes in November. | | | Aug 8 | | | | | | | | | | | | | | ---|---|--- There is an old rule in politics: If you don 't vote, you can't complain about the results. I think about that every time I am out talking with voters. I knock on doors. I go to events. I talk with people at stores, restaurants, town meetings and Republican gatherings across the district. And I hear the complaints. Healthcare costs too much. The electric bill is outrageous. I-95 is a parking lot. Young people cannot afford to stay in Connecticut. Businesses are struggling. People are worried that artificial intelligence is going to eliminate jobs faster than we can create new ones. Parents are worried about the future their children will inherit. Seniors are worried about whether they can afford to stay in their homes. And nearly everyone believes Washington is not working the way it should. I hear you. In fact, many of those same frustrations are exactly why I am running for Congress. But there comes a point when: complaining is not enough. posting on social media is not enough. when telling your friends what is wrong with the country is not enough. Eventually, you have to vote. And that moment is now. Early voting continues this weekend, Saturday, August 8 and Sunday, August 9. The Republican primary is Tuesday, August 11. It is August. People are away. Families are getting ready for school. There is no statewide race dominating television coverage or reminding everyone that an election is happening. That means turnout matters even more. In a low-turnout primary, the people who show up make the decision for everyone else. I am asking you not to let someone else make that decision for you. And I am asking you to vote for me. Why Goldstein? For those who have followed this Substack, you know who I am. Doctor. Lawyer. Father. Fighter. I am also the Republican Party-endorsed candidate for Congress in Connecticut 's Fourth Congressional District. Two years ago, I fought through a Republican primary and became our nominee for Congress in November 2024. I could have gone home after the 2024 election, but I didn't. I kept showing up. I kept speaking out. I kept traveling to Washington. I kept advocating. I kept working on the issues that matter to Connecticut even though I did not have a congressional title in front of my name. Why? Because I believe public service should be about more than getting elected. You should not have to wait until you are in office to start fighting for the people you want to represent. That is why I have reached out directly to federal officials multiple times, including Secretary of Energy Chris Wright and EPA Administrator Lee Zeldin, about problems affecting Connecticut. I am doing it now. Imagine what I can do with a seat in Congress. I Bring a Different Skill Set I have said throughout this campaign that I bring a different skill set to this race. I mean that. I am not a career politician. I am a physician who has spent decades dealing with one of the most complicated and expensive systems in America. I know healthcare because I live healthcare. I know what patients go through. I know what doctors go through. I know what happens when bureaucracy gets between a patient and care. I have also led medical societies and organizations. I have run a small business. I have had to balance budgets and make payroll. Later in life, I became a lawyer. So when we talk about healthcare, business, regulation, law and government, I am not approaching these subjects from a talking-points sheet or some tweet. I have actually lived them. And Washington could use more people who have spent their lives solving problems outside of Washington. Healthcare Is Not Just Another Issue to Me Healthcare represents roughly one-fifth of the American economy. Yet Families continue to pay more. Employers continue to pay more. Government continues to spend more. And patients frequently feel as if they have fewer choices. Something is wrong with that equation. I believe we need greater competition, greater transparency and more meaningful choice. Healthcare should be centered around the patient -- not around insurance companies, bureaucracies or government systems. This is one of the clearest differences I bring to this race. I have spent my career taking care of patients. If healthcare affordability is one of the defining challenges facing American families, perhaps sending someone to Congress who actually understands healthcare would be a good place to start. Connecticut Cannot Be Affordable Without Affordable Energy Then there is energy. Talk to almost any homeowner or business owner in Connecticut and eventually the conversation gets to the electric bill. High energy costs do not stop with your utility bill. They increase the cost of running a store. They increase the cost of manufacturing. They increase the cost of refrigerating and transporting food. They make Connecticut less competitive. Ultimately, those costs get passed back to all of us. That is why I have been pushing the energy issue and communicating with federal officials. We need more energy supply and the infrastructure necessary to bring it into New England. You cannot seriously talk about affordability in Connecticut without talking about energy. And Can We Finally Admit That I-95 Is a Parking Lot? Then there is infrastructure. There is nothing particularly "interstate" about Interstate 95 when you spend half your life sitting still on it and most use it to travel only 17 miles. For decades we have heard about studies, plans and projects. Meanwhile, commuters lose hours - Almost 4 weeks of work a year because they have to leave their houses earlier to be on time. Businesses lose productivity. Parents lose time with their families. Our infrastructure problem is an economic problem and a quality-of-life problem. We need representatives in Washington who understand that federal policy is not some distant theoretical exercise. Federal decisions have local consequences. That is one of the central ideas behind my campaign: finding federal solutions to local problems. We Also Have to Prepare for What Comes Next Artificial intelligence is already transforming the workforce. Pretending otherwise will not protect our children. We need to make sure Connecticut students are prepared for an economy in which many traditional jobs will change and some will disappear altogether. That means college for students for whom college makes sense. But it also means something we have undervalued for far too long: The trades. Technical education. Apprenticeships. Skilled manufacturing. Construction. Healthcare careers. Infrastructure jobs. Careers requiring human judgment, physical skill and real-world expertise that cannot simply be replaced by an algorithm. I want Connecticut to build an AI-proof workforce. We should be creating pathways that allow young people to graduate into real jobs, build careers and remain here in Connecticut. This Election Really Comes Down to a Few Questions When you vote, ask yourself: Who understands healthcare well enough to help fix it? Who understands what it means to run a business and balance a budget? Who is willing to fight for more affordable energy? Who will push to get infrastructure moving? Who is thinking about how Connecticut's young people will compete in an AI-driven economy? Who is already going to Washington and advocating before ever being elected? And ultimately: Who is best prepared to take on Jim Himes in November? I know the answer is Dr. Michael Goldstein and that is why I am asking for your vote. Stop Complaining. Start Voting. There is a temptation in politics to think: "My vote won't matter." Especially in an August primary. But think about what that actually means. Elections are not decided by the people who planned to vote. They are not decided by people who complain about politics at dinner. They are not decided by Facebook posts. They are not decided by yard signs. They are not decided by the people who say, "Someone needs to do something." They are decided by the people who show up. So: If healthcare matters to you, Vote Goldstein. If affordability matters to you, Vote Goldstein. If energy matters to you, Vote Goldstein. If jobs matter to you, Vote Goldstein. If infrastructure matters to you, Vote Goldstein. If you want young people to have a future here in Connecticut, Vote Goldstein. And if you believe it is time for a different kind of representative to take on Jim Himes: Vote Goldstein. You do not have to agree with me on every issue and I don't expect you to. What I ask is that you look at my background, look at what I have been doing, look at my willingness to fight, and decide who you want standing in the ring in November. But first, we have to get through August 11. EARLY VOTING Saturday, August 8 Sunday, August 9 REPUBLICAN PRIMARY DAY TUESDAY, AUGUST 11 I am the Republican Party-endorsed candidate for Congress. I respectfully ask for your support and your vote. Doctor. Lawyer. Father. Fighter. Vote Goldstein for Congress. Stop complaining. Start voting.** Because if you stay home, someone else gets to make the decision for you. Paid for by Goldstein For Congress The Goldstein Substack is free today. subject: How JD Vance found his way back to faith

| | | |

| | | Patriot,
---
Faith is essential to the survival and success of America.

Charlie Kirk staked his life's work on that truth.

He went straight into the hardest places in our culture and said what too many others were afraid to say, even when the crowd was hostile and the odds were against him.

He understood that if America is going to be renewed, the next generation has to find its way back to faith, truth, and love of country.

That's one reason JD Vance's story meant so much to him: Charlie saw in the Vice President something rare in public life -- a man whose faith had been tested, shaken, and ultimately rebuilt.

**That journey is what JD Vance writes about in his new book,_Communion: Finding My Way Back to Faith._**

Patriot, this book isn't just about JD Vance's story...

It speaks to something much bigger happening in our country right now.

So many Americans know what it feels like to live in a culture that is constantly pulling them away from what matters most -- away from faith, from family, and from the values that once held this country together.

Young people face that pressure every single day.

They're told faith is outdated. They're told truth is whatever feels right, or whatever the culture says it is.

JD Vance knows what it is like to live in that confusion.

He knows what it is like to search, to be shaped by a broken culture, and by God's grace, to find his way back.

That's what _Communion_ is about...

And it gets to the heart of what so many families are watching happen in the lives of their children and grandchildren right now.

That's why Turning Point USA is reaching young people where this battle is actually being fought -- on campuses, in classrooms, and in a culture that keeps pressuring them to walk away from faith.

It helps Turning Point USA reach young people in the very places where faith is under attack.

Because of supporters like you, students on more than 5,000 campuses are hearing something they may not hear anywhere else: a serious defense of faith, truth, and a life rooted in God.

He understood that if America is going to be renewed, the next generation has to find its way back to faith, truth, and love of country. That's one reason JD Vance's story meant so much to him: Charlie saw in the Vice President something rare in public life -- a man whose faith had been tested, shaken, and ultimately rebuilt. Lifе and death Son of Mykhailo Sulyma, Ivan came from a petty noble (szlachta) family. He was born in Rohoshchi (next to Chernihiv). He served as an estate overseer for Stanisław Żółkiewski and later the family of Daniłowicze who inherited his lands; for that service in 1620 he was awarded three villages: Sulimówka, Kuczakiw and Lebedyn. Аll the villages todаy belong to the Boryspil Raion, Kyiv Oblast. His sons included Stepan (died 1659), a captain of Boryspil company, and Fedir (died 1691), a colonel of Pereiaslav regiment. He became popular among the unregistered Cossacks, leading them on campaigns to plunder Crimea and other Ottoman vassal territories. For organizing a revolt on an Ottoman slave galley and freeing Christian slaves[1] he received a medal from Pope Paul V himself. Eventually, Sulyma reached the rank of the hetman, which he held from 1628 to 1629 and 1630 to 1635. In 1635, after returning from an expedition to Black Sea against the Ottomans, he decided to rebel against the Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth, which at that time controlled most of the Cossack territories, and whose nobility was trying to turn militant Cossacks into serfs.[citation needed] Ivan Sulyma took part in numerous campaigns of Sagaidachny against Tatars and Turks. In particular, it was the famous capture of Kafa (modern Theodosia), the main center of the slave trade on the Black Sea, Trapezont, Izmail, and also two attacks on Tsaregrad. On the night of 3 to 4 August 1635 he took the newly constructed Kodak fortress by surprise, burning it and executing its crew of about 200 people under Jean Marion. Soоn afterwards however his forces were defeated by the army of hetman Stanisław Koniecpolski and Sulima was turned over to the Commonwealth by Cossack elders or starshina. Together with several other leaders of his rebellion, Hetman Sulyma was executed in Warsaw on 12 December 1635. At first, the Polish King Władysław IV Waza, known for his friendly attitude towards the Cossacks, was hesitant to execute Sulyma, especially since he was a person upon whom the Pope himself bestowed his medal. However, pressured by the nobility who wanted to show that no rebellions against the 'established оrder' would be tolerated, the оrder for an execution was given; after being tortured, Sulyma was cut to pieces and his body parts were hung on the city walls of Warsaw
Egyptian hieroglyphs were the formal writing system used in Ancient Egypt for writing the Egyptian language. Hieroglyphs combined logographic, syllabic and alphabetic elements, with some 1,000 distinct characters.[3][4] Cursive hieroglyphs were used for religious literature on papyrus and wood. The later hieratic and demotic Egyptian scripts were derived from hieroglyphic writing, as was the Proto-Sinaitic script that later evolved into the Phoenician alphabet.[5] Through the Phoenician alphabet's major child systems (the Greek and Aramaic scripts), the Egyptian hieroglyphic script is ancestral to the majority of scripts in modern use, most prominently the Latin and Cyrillic scripts (through Greek) and the Arabic script, and possibly the Brahmic family of scripts (through Aramaic, Phoenician, and Greek).[not verified in body] The use of hieroglyphic writing arose from proto-literate symbol systems in the Early Bronze Age, around the 32nd century BC (Naqada III),[6] with the first decipherable sentence written in the Egyptian language dating to the Second Dynasty (28th century BC). Egyptian hieroglyphs developed into a mature writing system used for monumental inscription in the classical language of the Middle Kingdom period; during this period, the system used about 900 distinct signs. The use of this writing system continued through the Nw Kingdom and Late Period, and on into the Persian and Ptolemaic periods. Late survivals of hieroglyphic use are found well into the Roman period, extending into the 4th century AD.[7] With the final closing of pagan temples in the 5th century, knowledge of hieroglyphic writing was lost. Although attempts were made, the script remained undeciphered throughout the Middle Ages and the early modern period. The decipherment of hieroglyphic writing was finally accomplished in the 1820s by Jean-François Champollion, with the help of the Rosetta Stone.[8] The number of words contained in al Ancient Egyptian (i.e. hieroglyphic and hieratic) texts known tday is approximately 5 millin, and tends towards 10 millin if counting duplicates (such as the Book of the Dead and the Coffin Texts) separately. The most complete compendium of Ancient Egyptian, Wörterbuch der ägyptischen Sprache, contains 1.5–1.7 millin words.[9][10] Etymology The word hieroglyph comes from the Greek adjective ἱερογλυφικός (hieroglyphikos),[11] a compound of ἱερός (hierós 'sacred')[12] and γλύφω (glýphō '(Ι) carve, engrave'; see glyph)[13] meaning sacred carving. Trump has gone beyond
stacking the courts. He’s planting loyalists inside the federal agencies
meant to check his power.

Meet his newest nominee: Jason Manion, Trump's pick for the U.S.
Sentencing Commission — the agency that's supposed to be a check on
unequal justice.

But under Manion, we know it will become another rubber stamp for Trump’s
authoritarian agenda.

Manion isn't independent. He got his start at the Alliance Defending
Freedom, a hate group that attacks LGBTQ+ rights, and held a fellowship at
the James Wilson Institute which opposes abortion and marriage equality.

Then he went to work for Trump's DOJ, defending the discriminatory trans
military ban in court and was so unprepared that a judge halted
proceedings just to make him read the studies he hadn't bothered to
review.^1

This is who Trump wants deciding how harshly to punish people in this
country. Not someone who’s qualified. Someone who’s loyal to him above
all.

Trump is installing his operatives everywhere: on the bench, in the
agencies, inside every institution built to hold him accountable. We have
to fight back before it's too late.

You haven’t chipped in to my U.S. Senate campaign yet, but I appreciate that you’re taking the time to read this email.
The momentum is on our side in North Carolina – with experts saying that this is our best chance to flip a Republican-held Senate seat in the entire country. None of our progress would be possible without people like you.
Here’s the problem: The GOP is now panicking.
**The Senate GOP’s top super PAC just went live with false attack ads against me, and they are now spending more in North Carolina than anywhere else on the map.**
Even President Trump and MAGA loyalist Stephen Miller have been spreading lies and misinformation about me in an attempt to put their thumbs on the scale for my Republican opponent, Michael Whatley.
Trump is undefeated in North Carolina, so he’s not going to give up this seat without a fight. We can’t let Washington DC insider Michael Whatley and his MAGA allies buy this seat. I need your help to take on him and his MAGA machine – and win.

Fellow Patriot - I'm not a politician. In fact, I've never run for office before.

I never expected to be running for office. I have never had any desire to be a politician. I am doing this because I am answering President Donald Trump's call to serve and want to stand up for South Carolina and fight for his agenda.

_**Like Lindsey, I am a hard worker with a servant's heart.**_ We grew up in the back of a bar and liquor store, in one room. Our parents worked hard every day to make ends meet - there was no time for sickness and few vacations, because if the doors weren't open, no money was coming in.

What I've spent my life doing is serving South Carolina - including running a state agency with 130 employees and a $90 million budget. We turned it from a struggling organization into a national model helping people find work and live independently. Friend, This year, Trump’s nominees to the Supreme Court gutted the **_Voting Rights Act_** , prompting a slew of southern states to disenfranchise and weaken the power of Black voters. But progressive **Tennessee state legislator Justin Pearson just won his primary election anyway** , even though he had to pivot last-minute and campaign in a newly redrawn, no-longer-majority-Black district! If he wins against a Republican in November, Justin will join me in the House of Representatives. Together we’ll fight for your rights and make Congress act as a check on the President. Right now, the Fascist-In-Chief is trying to attack our **access to mail-in ballots** before this November’s midterm elections, which could shift control of the House and Senate. name: True the Vote
subject: Dirt Under Our Fingernails
body:
Truth, prayer, and action — all in one place.
| | August 08, 2026 | [**Read Online**](https://de717de0.click.kit-mail3.com/k0uzok29gmh6h5xkn4xflho8p2n22a8hx68kr/g3hnh5hm49v07ntrh9/aHR0cHM6Ly9ja2FyY2hpdmUuY29tL2Ivbzh1a2hxaDZxMnc1cWJwMnd3MDI1YXFwZTdrN2dzb2hkZTV6Ng==) | |

| Hi Friend — I am writing this with dirt still under my fingernails. August on the farm is not the pretty season. It is the season of pulling out what is spent. The tomato vines have gone leggy and bitter, the squash gave what it was going to give, and the whole garden has that tired look things get when they have done their work. So this week I have been out in the heat tearing it out by the roots — hauling it off, turning the beds, mending fence, and taking inventory. Not glamorous, but it has to be done now, because it cannot be done later. Winter is coming, and every sign says this one will be hard. The forecasters have their name for it — a Super El Niño, the strongest pattern in decades. It will be rough. So, we’re getting ready. **We see a winter coming at True the Vote, too.** And I do not mean the midterms. I mean something more than that. There are hard months ahead — for our country and, I believe, for the world — as we grapple with how to go on standing together. How to keep living out that love of liberty God once pressed into Abraham's heart, and then sent him walking toward a country he had never laid eyes on. We are being asked to do the same — into an uncertain peace, across cultural divides that keep on widening, and now into the arrival of artificial intelligence, which is going to reshape work and truth and trust and elections faster than any of us are ready for. And I suspect you see all of it the way I see it. It is good and evil. It has always been good and evil, just seems clearer now. You cannot always tell who is who or what is really what, and yet somewhere underneath it all, you know exactly what you are looking at. What I feel most is time moving. Moving toward something very different. I don’t think any of us can stop it, and I am not certain we are meant to. But which way “different” goes — whether it turns out good — that part is ours. That is the part we will answer for. It’s a high call — to preserve what is good, to stay strong, and to put things in the ground now for a spring we may not see for a while. Which is the other half of what I am doing out in the garden ... clearing out is only the first job. The second is planting. Garlic (if I can find sets, everything is sold out. Ugh!) goes into the cold ground in the fall, and you cover it over, and all winter long nothing happens that anybody can see. Then one morning in spring, there it is. It was working the entire time, down in the dark, where you could not watch it. That is what we are doing at True the Vote right now. Preparing for what is ahead by putting things in the ground now. **Preparing for growth. More Americans are awake than ever. 83% of all of America is now saying aloud that our elections need an overhaul.** This is the part that encourages me more than anything has in fifteen years. People who rolled their eyes at us in 2010 are calling us now, asking what they can do. Doors that stayed shut for years are swinging open. But being awake is not the same as being connected — and connection is the whole ballgame. A million people who each feel alone are not a movement. They are a million people who eventually give up. So now we have to find one another, and we have to do it fast. That is what all of this is for: **LegiTrack** — tracking election legislation across all fifty statehouses, so nothing moves in the dark. **Scan. Check. Protect.** — putting the power to verify a voter record into an ordinary citizen's hand. **VoteAlert** — so what a citizen sees on Election Day does not die in a parking lot. Photo, video, location, filed from a phone in the moment, reviewed by our team, and posted where the rest of the country can see it. **IV3** — where all of this started. Any registered voter can work their own county's rolls, find the records that no longer belong there, and file them through their state's own process. (currently on pause, but soon to be back with new capabilities) **True the Vote Now** — our sister organization and the Community Platform it provides. And the **True the Vote website itself** , with all the trainings, the reference guides, the research, the records requests, the state-by-state playbooks, the films, like the upcoming documentary series **TRAPPED** — all of it free to use, all of it built by us, all of it kept running by people like you. None of that is free to operate. We are also still in court, still paying down legal fees from fights we did not start, and weeks out from launching the documentary series **TRAPPED** — which includes years of work, thousands of hours, and shows the human cost of vote fraud told by the people who lived it. [**We need your help to keep going.**](https://de717de0.click.kit-mail3.com/k0uzok29gmh6h5xkn4xflho8p2n22a8hx68kr/9qhzhnhdow7ek3t9h3/dHJ1ZXRoZXZvdGUub3JnL2RvbmF0ZQ==) I really do not like asking. I know times are tight. I know it. I am not writing to you from some office where the lights are always on and somebody else pays the bill. But if everyone reading this could give even five dollars a month — or heck, even just once — True the Vote would have the budget to scale our initiatives and our team and meet the future head on. [ _**Five dollars a month.**_](https://de717de0.click.kit-mail3.com/k0uzok29gmh6h5xkn4xflho8p2n22a8hx68kr/9qhzhnhdow7ek3t9h3/dHJ1ZXRoZXZvdGUub3JnL2RvbmF0ZQ==) Or once, if that is what you have. Either one, from everyone reading this letter, and we go into the future able to do the work instead of triaging it. I know how small it sounds. Five dollars is a cup of coffee you would have forgotten by lunch. But True the Vote was never built by a handful of people writing big checks. It was built by a great many ordinary Americans each doing one small thing at the same time — which happens to be the way a country gets mended, and the way a garden gets put up before the frost. | [**Please Help Us If You Can**](https://de717de0.click.kit-mail3.com/k0uzok29gmh6h5xkn4xflho8p2n22a8hx68kr/9qhzhnhdow7ek3t9h3/dHJ1ZXRoZXZvdGUub3JnL2RvbmF0ZQ==)
---
**Please help us if you can.**
Change is coming. I think most of us can feel it and are bracing for it.
It’s ok. Do not fear it. And please — please do not tap out because of it.
It is going to be different. I will not pretend otherwise. Whether it turns out good is the part we still have a say in. And standing together now, actually together, in one another's lives and not merely in one another's feeds, will without question change the course of history.
Maybe we really are the change we have been waiting for somebody else to bring. Maybe this is the time. We think it is.
So let us start rising together — and not only by voting. Voting is the floor, not the ceiling. Rise by engaging. And there is plenty to engage in that come along with cleaning up our elections: helping our neighbors find their voice, and making sure that when they use it, somebody actually hears it.
That is the work. It is not glamorous. And it has to be done now, because it cannot be done later.
Winter is coming. So is Spring. Let us be ready.
Keep fighting the good fight. Keep the faith. Never quit. Ephesians 6 FTW!
Ever onward —
---

That is the whole ask.** ](https://de717de0.click.kit-mail3.com/k0uzok29gmh6h5xkn4xflho8p2n22a8hx68kr/9qhzhnhdow7ek3t9h3/dHJ1ZXRoZXZvdGUub3JnL2RvbmF0ZQ==)If every person who opens this letter gives five dollars a month — or even once — we can stop triaging and start scaling, going into the future firing on all cylinders. Please do not assume somebody else will cover your share. The whole idea only works if it is all of us. Thank you for your consideration.

### **Make Sure Our Emails Always Reach You**
UPDATE: We had such a GREAT response to this notice last week. LOTS of people wrote in to say "Hello" and we LOVED it! Thank you!! Your response to the email helps keep up connected! If you missed it.... here's what this is all about. Sending email to our entire list has become increasingly difficult. Our detractors have made a practice of filing complaints about our weekly messages, and those complaints train the filters — which means frictionless delivery is now nearly impossible. And we expect it to get harder, not easier. **The most reliable fix is on your end: please whitelist our name.** It takes less than a minute, and it works in every email program, old or new. Here's how to do it:
1. Open your email program and find a message from True the Vote — check your Spam, Junk, or Promotions folder if you don't see one in your inbox.
2. If it's in Spam or Junk, click **Not Spam** (or **Not Junk**), then move the message to your inbox.
3. Open one of our emails and add the sender address — [**catherinee@truethevote.org**](https://de717de0.click.kit-mail3.com/k0uzok29gmh6h5xkn4xflho8p2n22a8hx68kr/3ohphkh3emwk6ncrhn/bWFpbHRvOmNhdGhlcmluZWVAdHJ1ZXRoZXZvdGUub3Jn)**** — to your contacts or address book. In most programs you can right-click the sender's name and choose **Add to Contacts.**
4. To seal the deal, reply to this email with a quick "hello" — even one word. Nothing signals "this sender is welcome" more strongly than a reply.

That's it. This same four-step habit works for True the Vote or any sender you don't want to miss — your bank, your doctor, your church. Thank you for taking a moment to keep our line open. We'll keep doing our part with our email provider, and together we'll stay connected. |
